notes: Market wave (D6): 40 bundles in six phases, M0 to M5, that implement every requirement of docs/jobright-clone/market/MARKET_STRATEGY.md section 9 which code can deliver. The strategy is decisive; where an item disagrees with it the strategy wins (say so in the handoff). The GoApply parity wave (docs/jobright-clone/orch/parity-bundles.json) is merged first and already covers JC-1, the interim JC-2 reader, JC-4 routing and first seed, JC-7, the linkedin line of JI-2, AL-1, AL-2, AL-5, the GoApply half of PC-1 and PC-2: items here verify that code, they do not rebuild it. Companion document with the phase table, hot-file owners, cross-bundle contracts, schema list, env variables, owner list and the coverage table: docs/jobright-clone/market/MARKET_TASK_PLAN.md.

Phases run in order; bundles of one phase run in parallel in separate worktrees. M0 = MKT-0 (schema only; merged, then the orchestrator runs server/prisma/sql/001_vector.sql and pushes the additive diff to the database branch before anything else starts). M1 = rollout phase A (Stripe safety, catalog and checkout; pricing page; Taiwan pay parser and source contracts; evaluation harness; taxonomy precision; estimate v2 and the fit contract; documents and env examples). M2 = phase B billing (Alipay wire parity, Stripe lifecycle, refunds, billing UI) and the match foundations (every consumer on getFit, skill vocabulary, search document and embeddings). M3 = phase B job sources (quota, planner, posting identity, employer boards, Taiwan open data, provider health, mainland deep links) and the runbooks. M4 = billing phase B consumers (withdrawal endpoints, admin billing, UI) and match phases C and D (enrichment v3, skills in the estimate, hybrid retrieval, scorer v4, search surfaces). M5 = job-source phases C and D (licensed feed, connectors, closure, new public sources, GoHire syndication, Taiwan extras, sponsorship facts) and the final documents. Five work phases instead of three because the three domain drafts held 15 and 16 bundles in their second and third phases and a phase carries at most 8.

Traceability to the domain drafts in docs/jobright-clone/orch/market-plan/ (billing.json, sources.json, match.json): MKT-1A = B1, 1B = B2, 1C = J1, 1D = S1, 1E = S2, 1F = S3; MKT-2A..2E = B3..B7, 2F = S4, 2G = S5, 2H = S6; MKT-3A..3G = J2..J8, 3H = B11; MKT-4A = B8, 4B = B9, 4C = B10, 4D = S7, 4E = S8, 4F = S9, 4G = S10, 4H = S11; MKT-5A..5G = J9..J15; MKT-0 folds S0 and the schema arrays of B6, B8, J4, J5 and J15; MKT-1G and MKT-5H are new (documents and env examples). Item text is the planners' except for the corrections listed in the companion document under "Changes made in consolidation".

Ownership is disjoint inside every phase: no path in two bundles, no owned directory containing another bundle's path, no i18n namespace owned twice (node docs/jobright-clone/orch/check-bundles.mjs docs/jobright-clone/orch/market-bundles.json reports 0 problems). New files inside an owned directory and tests colocated with owned files are yours. Anything else is a Request in the handoff, addressed to the owning bundle id or to the orchestrator; never edit a file you do not own.

Hot files, one owner per phase. server/src/platform/flags.ts and flags.test.ts: MKT-1A in M1 (one line at case pay.stripe and one import), nobody afterwards. server/src/cron/handlers.ts, vercel.json and deploy/cn/k8s/cronjobs.yaml: MKT-3D in M3 (the jobs-boards cron), nobody in any other phase: calibration, the retrieval sweep, the licensed feed and the Taiwan sweep run as steps or cursor sources of existing cron jobs. server/src/features/index.ts: MKT-5F in M5 (mounts features/tw), nobody before: every other new route is added to a router that is already mounted. package.json: MKT-1D in M1 (one script line, eval:match), nobody afterwards; no bundle adds an npm dependency. .env.example and deploy/cn/cn.env.example: MKT-1G in M1 and MKT-5H in M5. i18n/staging/index.ts: MKT-5G in M5 (registers companyFacts). server/src/app.ts, server/src/platform/brand/, components/v3/shell/destinations.ts and lib/proxyPaths.ts: no owner in any phase, because no item needs them; if you find you need a line there, write a Request and do not edit.

Env variables: every bundle lists its variables in its env array. Only MKT-1G (M1 variables) and MKT-5H (everything later) edit .env.example and deploy/cn/cn.env.example. Every other engineer lists new or redefined variables in the handoff section "Env variables added or redefined" (name, meaning, default) and that is all: it is not a Request. Never print or commit a secret value and do not open .env.

Schema: engineers of M1 to M5 never edit *.prisma and never run db push, migrate, DDL or DML. Everything a bundle needs is in its schema array and is delivered by MKT-0. From M1 on the code selects the new RAJob columns in its projections, so every database needs the M0 push before it runs that code (the Neon branch first, each deployment database before its deploy). Embedding rows are read and written with $queryRaw / $executeRaw; RAJob.searchTsv is written by the application in the same statement as searchDoc.

Stripe safety (ST-0): the clone .env holds a live Stripe key. MKT-1A does its first item first: the guard lives in the one client factory getStripe, so no Stripe call of any kind is attempted with a live key outside production. Every Stripe test uses setStripeClientForTests, setBillingServiceDepsForTests or an injected fake; no item calls Stripe, the GoHire worker, a model, an embeddings endpoint, a job provider or a database.

Alipay strictness (D6, strategy 5.2): server/src/platform/billing/rails/alipayWorker.ts is edited only by MKT-2A and only additively; fulfilPass.ts, the callback route and handleAlipayCallback are edited by no bundle in any phase; AlipayOrder is not changed by MKT-0; the A1 to A12 characterisation tests written by the parity wave stay green and unedited (adding STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET to a shared env fixture at the top of a test file is the only permitted touch near them, MKT-1A; the three assertions AL-3 changes on purpose are not A-tests and are named in MKT-2A item 1). The A-tests as the parity wave built them (43 tests named 'A<number> …', listed in docs/jobright-clone/orch/handoffs-par/PAR-6.md) are strict in four places that shape this plan: the Stripe rail must refuse a GoApply order with plan_not_sellable before any Stripe call (MKT-1A keeps a brand check in the rail now that GoApply plans are sellable); a callback with a valid secret must resolve on a database that throws, so the amount tolerance reads the order only when the value can be a fen amount (MKT-2A); a GoApply-branded Stripe session keeps answering handled true (MKT-2B); and the history rows are compared with toEqual, so the two new invoice fields are optional and omitted when they add nothing (MKT-4B, MKT-4C). A change that makes a test named 'A<number> …' fail is wrong: rework the change or write a Request; never edit the test. AL-7 reverses entitlements in its own admin service (MKT-4B).

Billing file owners per phase: server/src/platform/billing/index.ts M1 MKT-1A, M2 MKT-2D, M4 nobody (a bundle that adds a module without owning index.ts imports it by file path); RoboApplyBillingService.ts and roboapply/routes/billing.ts M1 MKT-1A, M2 MKT-2B, M4 MKT-4B; features/credits/{routes,service,contract}.ts M1 MKT-1A, M2 MKT-2C, M4 MKT-4A; components/features/credits/, hooks/credits/ and the credits and billingCn namespaces M1 MKT-1B, M2 MKT-2E, M4 MKT-4C. Server and web halves of one requirement run in the same phase in different bundles, so the web bundle writes request and response types by hand from the contract text repeated in both items (lib/api/account.ts, lib/api/adminBilling.ts). It must not add documented wrappers to lib/api/credits.ts or mirrored contract types for a route built in parallel: __tests__/contracts/fixtures.test.ts checks every documented wrapper against the server mount table and would fail in the web worktree.

Billing design choices that go beyond the strategy text (flagged for the owner in the companion document): the refund lines on /pricing take their numbers from a new refundPolicy object on GET /billing/plans and GoApply's entity from checkout.collectingEntity (additive fields); a refunded pass is reversed by subtracting its length from the end date, because passes stack; Stripe Checkout custom_text is English in this wave (the localized, recorded consent is on our own plan sheet); the full webhook-endpoint readout is in the credits console and the admin System panel shows the summary line with a link (MKT-4B serves it, MKT-4C renders both). Findings beyond the strategy: RAAdminOperationsService.ts built a second Stripe client that bypassed the factory (MKT-1A routes it through getStripe and adds a source-scan test); account deletion cascades away the renewal acknowledgement before the AB 2863 period ends (MKT-4A archives a minimal proof in RABillingConsentArchive).

Job sources: MKT-1C carries inert contracts besides the Taiwan pay parser (provider ids tw_open_data, tw_gov_jobs, usajobs, activejobs_feed; optional costModel and isEnabledFor on the adapter interface; optional input fields; the quota snapshot contract; the User-Agent helper; the optional zhHant label type) so the M3 bundles never compile against each other. Contracts inside M3 that have no compile dependency and are verified after the M3 merge: MKT-3C writes RAJob.atsPostingKey and MKT-3D's discovery reads it from the hook object as a plain string; MKT-3B plans a Taiwan tuple with Traditional Chinese text and MKT-3A's rapidApiSearchParams turns it into a zh-TW query; MKT-3A fills NormalizeContext.companyDomains and MKT-3C reads it; MKT-3A hands the query's country to nextRunDelayMs through a variable and MKT-3B adds the optional RefreshInput.country (hot demand 6 h, cold demand 24 h, Taiwan 12 h: strategy 1.2 tier 2 and 1.3); MKT-3A writes AppConfig jobs.providerQuota.v1 and MKT-3F reads it through MKT-1C's parser; MKT-3E's adapter sets ProviderJobInput.taxonomyId and MKT-1C's normalizer honours it; MKT-3E returns exhausted false during a sweep and MKT-3A caps a cursor source's share of a tick; MKT-3D's board sync calls processJobs (signature unchanged by MKT-3A). After the M3 merge the orchestrator runs the acceptance lines of JI-5, JT-3 and JI-3 once, because each spans two bundles.

Job-source defaults chosen by the planner where the strategy gives no number (each a named constant with an env override; the owner may change them): 5% of a monthly quota reserved for interactive searches; a cursor source may use 40% of one ingest tick; board sync every 5 minutes with 6 listings in flight and intervals of 2 h, 12 h and 24 h; hard failures (404, redirect, wrong shape) count toward the three-failure disable while timeouts and 5xx only back off; the 台灣就業通 sweep makes 5 requests per fetch with a 1.5 s pause; source priorities usajobs 8, activejobs_feed 10, tw_open_data 12, tw_gov_jobs 12; INGEST_FEED_COUNTRIES default list; 北森 cap of 200 postings per tenant and run; liveness recheck after 6 hours; the mainland feed budget is 20% of the daily feed budget.

D3, D1 and the forbidden list hold in every bundle. Seed files contain only tenants a research note confirms (the 14 Taiwan boards, BoschGroup and Ubisoft2 for the mainland, stripe and ramp for the international backbone, plus what the parity engineer verified). Postal codes, 通俗職業 codes, deep-link URL patterns, vendor header names and government file headers are never typed from memory: each item says where the value must be read and what ships when it cannot be confirmed (an unverified deep link is not shown; the sweep uses its fallback split; the direct feed transport stays unconfigured). Synthetic fixtures are labelled SYNTHETIC; no real posting text, employer row or contact field is committed. No adapter fetches a source of strategy 1.6; JSearch stays off for GoApply; the 北森 connector cannot build a request while its flag is off. Nothing in this plan submits or pre-submits an application; the liveness check is one documented JSON read of a public posting.

Match: the seams that make later bundles independent are built early and stated in the items. Since MKT-1F the job projections carry the new columns, match/prepare.ts exists, and the wire types JobRequirement, RequirementCheck and MatchFitView.requirements exist. Since MKT-2H POST /feed/query accepts relevance and planToFilters returns rankedBy; retrieval/index.ts exports userVector, nearestJobsByJob and currentModelTag; the feed contract carries legLimit, rrfK, the order value query_match and FeedItem.alsoIn; the published ranking texts live in feed/rankingText.ts; sql.ts exports qPredicateSql and feed/index.ts exports similarJobIds. Several strategy items already exist on the branch from the verification fix groups (resume-based level, honesty caps, stored-AI-else-estimate for lists, the architect redirect, country-only locations, pay plausibility, GoApply fit-card wording, the Assistant's added-jobs tool): the items cite the code as it is and verify those instead of rebuilding them, which is why SM-10 needs no edit to normalize/salary.ts or feed/sql.ts.

Match interpretations and numbers the planner chose (each a named constant with an override; listed for the owner): invariant I3 is read strictly, so the estimate takes the person's role from resume and profile evidence and no longer from the saved search's role filter, and with no role evidence the title component takes its prior and confidence is low; logistics prior 50 (the one prior the strategy gives no number for); data-derived priors from 200 pairs and the calibration map from 500; related evidence counts half of an item; SKILL_EMBED_MATCH_MIN 0.86 with a 0.03 margin; seen-and-skipped 5 / 7.5 / 10 points; wrong-title weight -0.25; the dense leg switches model at 90% coverage; a typed query waits 800 ms for its vector. AI totals keep today's arithmetic; priors apply to the estimate only. The wire value kind: 'pre' is kept for an estimate so the published extension and the web keep working.

Evaluation harness gates (SM-1): the harness specs (eval/**/*.eval.ts) are outside npm test until a phase has merged, because the invariants are written to fail on the base commit. After the M1 merge the orchestrator runs "npm run eval:match -- --enforce M1" and it must exit 0; after M2 "--enforce M2" (MKT-2F puts nine invariants into npm test); after M4 "--enforce M4" (MKT-4E adds the tenth). The stage names of the harness are the phase names of this file. Committed fixtures are synthetic and say so; labels are named constructed, judged or human and are never mixed in a report.

Enrichment version bumps twice: 1 to 2 in M1 (MKT-1E: role override, industry) and 2 to 3 in M4 (MKT-4D: canonical skills, requirements, sponsorship source). Each re-enriches live rows gradually through jobs-maintain inside the existing daily enrichment budget; rows keep serving until their turn; the handoffs state the expected number of model calls. CLIs that touch a database (backfills, skills, retrieval backfill, the sponsor importers, eval --live) default to a dry run or refuse without an explicit flag and are run by the owner or the orchestrator, never by a work-package engineer.

Cross-domain points settled in consolidation (each is written into the item it concerns): MKT-4F owns feed/sql.ts and feed/contract.ts in M4 and makes the two changes the match draft had left as requests (case q of predicateFor uses the wide predicate so counts and alerts match the list; the unused freshness constant is deleted); MKT-5C owns FeedQueryService.ts in M5 and passes the last-visit instant itself; MKT-4D sets sponsorshipSource = posting_quote in enrichment, the other half of MKT-3C's carry-through rule; MKT-3B builds provider queries with providerQueryLabels from MKT-1E; MKT-4C shows the Stripe endpoint summary in the admin System panel that MKT-3F rebuilt one phase earlier; the same-role control stays its own component under the card and hybrid SQL stays in feed/hybridSql.ts, as the match draft designed them.

i18n: a namespace has one owner per phase. M1: credits and billingCn (MKT-1B), landing (MKT-1F: only landing.ranking.*). M2: credits and billingCn (MKT-2E), fit and tailor (MKT-2F). M3: jobsTw (MKT-3D), admin (MKT-3F), jobsCn with zh (MKT-3G). M4: credits, billingCn and admin (MKT-4C), fit (MKT-4E), jobs and landing (MKT-4F), assistant (MKT-4H). M5: jobDetail (MKT-5C), jobsTw and filters (MKT-5F), the new companyFacts (MKT-5G, registered in i18n/staging/index.ts). Mail strings are staged in English in server/src/i18n/email/staging/billing.en.json (MKT-2B) and billingRefunds.en.json (MKT-2D). OT-2 is the orchestrator's step after every phase: merge staging, translate into all locales, run npm run check. The zh-TW taxonomy labels are generated from taxonomy.v1.json through exportTaxonomyLabels (MKT-3E), not machine-translated. Board names, ATS names, attribution sentences, district names and 大類 names are server data, not bundle copy (the copy gate bans 牛客 and 北森 in zh copy).

Merge-time checks for the orchestrator. After M1: run the marketing page tests once more on the merged tree (MKT-1B owns components/features/marketing/__tests__/pages.test.tsx and MKT-1F changes the string landing.ranking.fit.body; a text assertion on the old sentence is fixed at merge). After M2: the cast in jobs/detail for similarJobIds (MKT-2F) meets its export (MKT-2H); run the Similar jobs test on the merged tree. After M3: the three cross-bundle acceptance lines of the job-source note above, and confirm the jobs-boards cron appears in vercel.json, cron/handlers.ts and the regenerated mainland CronJob file with the same schedule. After M4: npm run eval:match -- --enforce M4; the feed count and the list agree for a typed query. After M5: the env example test and the full gates (npm test, npm run typecheck:server, npm run typecheck:web, npm run check, npm run build when no dev server uses the same .next).
Line anchors in the items were verified on feat/jobright-clone before the parity wave merged, and each phase moves code again: find the code by symbol, do not trust the number.

Not planned, with the reason: JC-3 (the syndication route lives in the RoboHire / GoHire repository; this repository's side is MKT-5E) and the supervised AL-8 order (owner present; the script and the runbook are MKT-3H); the exploration slot of SM-12 (waits for the owner); a reranker and learned ranking weights; an HNSW or BM25 index; Lightcast data; a skills review UI (the CSV round trip of MKT-2G covers it); the LinkedIn Job Search API (M-4); a TheirStack adapter; Arbeitnow, Jobicy, RemoteOK and Reed (terms not confirmed in writing); Teamtailor, BambooHR, Moka and 飞书招聘 connectors; mainland partnership feeds; a real TWD price list (V2, off until PRICE_<KEY>_TWD_CENTS is set, which the catalog already reads); subtracting refunds in the admin payments report (no requirement names it; the data exists from M2).

Critic pass (2026-10-11), after the parity wave's PAR-6 handoff and tests existed in its worktree. Fixed in the items: MKT-1A (the Stripe rail and the catalog sync refuse a GoApply plan before any Stripe call: rule A11 as tested), MKT-2A (three non-A assertions named instead of one; amount tolerance without a database read unless the value can be fen; the secret-less window opens the database only inside a live window; order-number pattern), MKT-2B (handled true for a GoApply-branded session; a stored goapply row is never touched by a Stripe event: PAR-6 finding 10), MKT-4B and MKT-4C (history rows keep their exact shape; optional channel and refunded), MKT-3A and MKT-3B (cold demand refreshes every 24 h and Taiwan every 12 h, as strategy 1.2 and 1.3 say; the item had kept today's 12 h for cold demand), MKT-5A (adaptersForBrand must return the Active Jobs DB adapter for GoApply without editing the brand registry), MKT-5E (test postings are skipped on every bank transport), dependsOn of MKT-3E and MKT-5C. Checked and left as written: every price, label and key format of strategy 4 and 5.1; the fourteen webhook event types and their claims; rules G1 to G13; source tiers, cadences and the forbidden list; the fit invariants, priors and gates; the schema of M0 against the models on the branch; ownership of every FILES line. OT-2 has no bundle by design: work-package engineers may not edit i18n/messages, so merging staging, translating into the nine locales and npm run check is the orchestrator's step after each phase. MKT-3D is the heaviest bundle (seven items, the board sync engine among them). It stays one bundle because its items share contract.ts, service.ts, routes.ts, connectors.ts and ingest/boards.ts; if its engineer runs out of session, the bulk import (item 6, P1) is the item to hand to a follow-up bundle, never the seed files (item 7), which fill both feeds.

schema:
new model RASponsorRegisterEntry (end of server/prisma/schema/ra-jobs.prisma; no relation fields):
/// Public sponsor registers beside the DOL LCA table RAH1bEmployerStat: USCIS H-1B Employer Data Hub and the UK Register
/// of Licensed Sponsors. Company facts with source and date; never a job-level label. JI-11.
model RASponsorRegisterEntry {
  id                     String   @id @default(cuid())
  /// 'uscis_h1b_hub' | 'uk_sponsor_register'
  source                 String
  /// ISO alpha-2
  country                String
  employerNameNormalized String
  employerName           String
  /// 'FY2025' for USCIS, '' for the UK register
  period                 String   @default("")
  approvals              Int?
  denials                Int?
  town                   String?
  rating                 String?
  routes                 String[] @default([])
  sourceFile             String
  sourceUrl              String
  asOf                   DateTime
  importedAt             DateTime @default(now())

  @@unique([source, employerNameNormalized, period])
  @@index([country, employerNameNormalized])
}

new model RASkill (new file server/prisma/schema/ra-skills.prisma):
model RASkill {
  /// Stable slug, e.g. 'postgresql', 'relational_databases', 'cpa'.
  id             String   @id
  /// 'hard' | 'soft' | 'certification'
  kind           String   @default("hard")
  labelEn        String
  labelZh        String?
  labelZhHant    String?
  /// Comparison keys (features/match/terms.ts termKey form) of every label and alias in any script.
  aliases        String[] @default([])
  /// Broader skill this one is evidence for (postgresql -> relational_databases).
  parentId       String?
  esco           String?
  onet           String?
  /// 'reviewed' | 'unreviewed' (unreviewed skills are shown, never scored).
  status         String   @default("unreviewed")
  mentionCount   Int      @default(0)
  /// Label vector, written with raw SQL; embeddingModel says which model produced it.
  embedding      Unsupported("halfvec(1024)")?
  embeddingModel String?
  createdAt      DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt      DateTime @updatedAt
  @@index([aliases], type: Gin)
  @@index([parentId])
  @@index([status, mentionCount(sort: Desc)])
}

new models (new file server/prisma/schema/ra-retrieval.prisma); rows are read and written with $queryRaw / $executeRaw only:
model RAJobEmbedding {
  jobId       String   @id
  job         RAJob    @relation(fields: [jobId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  market      String
  /// e.g. 'openai/text-embedding-3-small@1024'
  model       String
  /// sha1 of the embedded card text
  contentHash String
  embedding   Unsupported("halfvec(1024)")
  embeddedAt  DateTime @default(now())
  @@index([market, model])
}
model RAUserEmbedding {
  userId     String
  user       User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  market     String
  /// 'intent' (onboarding and search answers) | 'resume' (primary resume)
  kind       String
  model      String
  sourceHash String
  embedding  Unsupported("halfvec(1024)")
  updatedAt  DateTime @default(now())
  @@id([userId, market, kind])
}

model RABillingRefund (new, server/prisma/schema/ra-credits.prisma; additive; no relation fields so no existing model is edited):
/// One refund, withdrawal, dispute or manual CN refund (MARKET_STRATEGY ST-4, ST-9, AL-7). Idempotency stays on
/// RACreditLedger claims; this row is the readable record (history marker, admin list, dispute flag). Insert-only.
model RABillingRefund {
  id                  String   @id @default(cuid())
  userId              String
  brand               String   // 'roboapply' | 'goapply'
  rail                String   // 'stripe' | 'alipay' | 'wechatpay'
  kind                String   // 'refund' | 'withdrawal' | 'dispute' | 'manual_cn'
  /// Stripe: '<chargeId>:<amount_refunded>' or 'dispute:<disputeId>'; CN: 'order:<AlipayOrder.id>'
  externalRef         String
  chargeId            String?
  paymentIntentId     String?
  invoiceId           String?
  checkoutSessionId   String?
  alipayOrderId       String?
  planKey             String?
  amountMinor         Int
  currency            String
  full                Boolean  @default(false)
  entitlementReversed Boolean  @default(false)
  reason              String?
  /// Admin user id, 'self' (withdrawal) or 'stripe' (Dashboard refund, dispute)
  actor               String?
  note                String?  @db.Text
  createdAt           DateTime @default(now())

  @@unique([rail, externalRef])
  @@index([userId, createdAt(sort: Desc)])
  @@index([invoiceId])
  @@index([alipayOrderId])
  @@index([kind, createdAt])
}

model RABillingConsentArchive (new, server/prisma/schema/ra-credits.prisma; additive; no relation fields):
/// Checkout acknowledgements kept after the account is deleted (California AB 2863: the later of 3 years after
/// consent and 1 year after the subscription ends). Written by the account purge, removed by compliance-daily. ST-9.
model RABillingConsentArchive {
  id                  String    @id @default(cuid())
  /// The deleted account's user id (no FK) and sha256 of its lower-cased email.
  userId              String
  emailHash           String
  brand               String
  consentType         String    // 'auto_renew_ack' | 'withdrawal_waiver' | 'cn_pay_terms_ack'
  proseHash           String?
  proseVersion        String?
  consentedAt         DateTime
  subscriptionEndedAt DateTime?
  stripeCustomerId    String?
  retainUntil         DateTime
  createdAt           DateTime  @default(now())

  @@index([retainUntil])
  @@index([emailHash])
  @@index([userId])
}

The third condition is new and necessary: since the parity wave a GoApply plan is sellable with a CNY amount, so the old refusal (its price id is null) no longer protects rule A11, and the parity wave's test 'A11 the Stripe rail refuses a GoApply order before it creates a customer or a session' (rails/rails.test.ts) pins exactly this answer (code plan_not_sellable; customers.create and checkout.sessions.create never called) and must pass unedited. 'TWD' : 'USD') (replaces line 85). ensureCustomer (56-69): customers.create(params, { idempotencyKey: 'customer:<seekerProfileId>' }). sessions.create (97-110) gains adaptive_pricing: { enabled: false }, locale (app locale mapped to a Stripe Checkout locale: en, zh, zh-TW, ja, ko, es, fr, de, pt -> pt-BR; anything else 'auto'), customer_update: { address: 'auto', name: 'auto' }, subscription_data.description (brand name + plan label) for subscriptions, and custom_text.submit.message repeating period, price and how to cancel: for a renewing plan "Renews every <period> at <price> until you cancel. Cancel any time in Settings or at <app origin>/cancel."; for the pass and packs "One payment of <price>. It does not renew." (built in code from the plan and the amount charged, in English in this wave; at most 1,200 characters). Second argument of sessions.create: { idempotencyKey: 'checkout:<userId>:<planKey>:<currency>:<attempt>' } where <attempt> is order.attemptKey when it matches /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}$/, else 'b' + floor(now / 60 s) (a 60-second bucket that only absorbs a double click; add now to StripeRailDeps). A Stripe idempotency error (same key, different parameters) maps to payment_provider_error with details.reason 'idempotency_conflict'. Existing rules stay untouched: acknowledgement recorded before Stripe opens, a pass refused while a plan renews, a subscription refused while any plan is live, the student gate, mode 'payment' with invoice_creation for the pass and packs, metadata on session, subscription and payment intent. server/src/roboapply/services/RoboApplyBillingService.ts: CheckoutInput (lines 308-322) gains attemptKey and locale, passed to rail.createCheckout (lines 417-429). server/src/roboapply/routes/billing.ts checkout() (lines 139-181): attemptKey = the Idempotency-Key request header (trimmed, same pattern, otherwise undefined); locale = the X-Robo-Locale header the web client already sends. env: STRIPE_ALLOW_LIVE_KEY_OUTSIDE_PRODUCTION: true lets a live Stripe key work when VERCEL_ENV is not production (default unset = refused)
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET / ROBOAPPLY_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET: now REQUIRED for the Stripe rail to be available; a comma-separated list is accepted (default unset = plans listed, payments_disabled)
PRICE_<PLANKEY>_USD_CENTS: overrides a RoboApply catalog amount, positive integer cents (default: catalog 999 / 2499 / 5499 / 999 / 999 / 2499 / 1749 / 3799)
STRIPE_PRICE_<PLANKEY>_CENTS: read as an alias of PRICE_<PLANKEY>_USD_CENTS (default unset)
STRIPE_PRICE_<PLANKEY>: optional pin of a Stripe price id, honoured only together with an amount variable (default unset = price resolved by the catalog sync)
PRICE_<PLANKEY>_TWD_CENTS: Taiwan price in TWD minor units, multiple of 100 (default unset = Taiwan pays USD with the reference line)
STRIPE_PRICE_<PLANKEY>_TWD_CENTS: alias of PRICE_<PLANKEY>_TWD_CENTS; STRIPE_PRICE_<PLANKEY>_TWD: optional pin (default unset)

Replace with keys in credits.pricing.refund.* whose numbers are ICU arguments filled from the new refundPolicy object of GET /billing/plans (contract, written identically in MKT-1A): refundPolicy: { firstPurchaseDays: 7, shortPlanHours: 48, paidOnlyCreditLimit: 5, accidentalRenewalDays: 3, withdrawalDays: 14, packValidMonths: 12, version: string }; read it through an optional structural type (the mirrored contract type gains the field when MKT-1A merges) and hide the section while it is absent. CHANGE: hooks/credits/useBillingActions.ts usePlanCheckout: PlanCheckoutVars gains attemptKey: string; lib/api/account.ts checkoutPlan(body, opts) and alipayCheckoutPlan(body, opts) pass { headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': attemptKey } } to roboApi.post (RequestOptions.headers exists, lib/api/client.ts:246). components/features/credits/PlanPicker.tsx: keep the attempt key in a ref created with crypto.randomUUID() when the sheet mounts and replaced whenever the selected plan or either acknowledgement box changes (the key must change when the request body changes, because Stripe refuses a repeated key with different parameters) and after a checkout call fails; a double click on Continue therefore sends the same key and the button is disabled while the call is pending (already so). CHANGE: Types and inert defaults only, so bundles that run in parallel later do not need each other's files. (1) server/src/features/jobs/normalize/types.ts: NormalizeProvider (line 13) becomes JobProvider | 'ats_public' | 'tw_open_data' | 'tw_gov_jobs' | 'usajobs' | 'activejobs_feed' (no edit to server/src/platform/brand/registry.ts). bundles.title: Evaluation harness, fixtures and the ten invariant specs, written first (SM-1)
items:
[P0] Runner, command and report: npm run eval:match offline, -- --live opt-in (SM-1; strategy 2.6; MATCH 6.5)
CHANGE: package.json: add the script "eval:match": "tsx server/src/features/match/eval/run.ts" (tsx is already a devDependency; nothing else in package.json changes). New vitest.eval.config.mts: same resolve aliases and closed-port DATABASE_URL / DIRECT_DATABASE_URL as vitest.config.mts (the env block at lines 29-32), environment node, include only server/src/features/match/eval/**/*.eval.ts, so the specs are NOT picked up by "npm test" (whose include is **/*.test.ts). New server/src/features/match/eval/run.ts: arguments --live, --enforce M1|M2|M4|all (default all), --market intl|cn|all, --suite <name>, --json <file>, --write-baseline. It (1) installs an offline guard unless --live (globalThis.fetch throws "network is off in eval"), (2) runs the invariant specs through the Vitest node API with the eval config and collects one result per invariant, (3) runs every suite found on disk under eval/suites/*.suite.ts; a suite exports { name, layer, run(ctx) } and loads its fixtures by path with fs at run time, never by a static import from outside eval/, so a later bundle can add suites/<x>.suite.ts and fixtures/<x>/ without editing the runner, (4) prints one table: layer, metric, value, gate, status where status is pass | fail | no_fixture | not_built | untrusted | skipped_offline, (5) exits 1 when an invariant whose due phase is at or before --enforce fails, or a suite that has fixtures misses its gate. New eval/README.md: how to add a suite and a fixture folder, the gate table, the two commands, and the rule that fixtures are synthetic.
ACCEPT: Accepted when (SM-1): npm run eval:match runs offline; the invariants fail before the fixes and pass after. Added: on the base commit the command needs no network and no database, prints the table and exits 1 naming each failing invariant with its reason; "npm run eval:match -- --enforce M1" is the command the orchestrator runs after the M1 merge and it must exit 0 then; npm test is unaffected by this bundle (no *.test.ts under eval/ fails).
TESTS: server/src/features/match/eval/run.test.ts: argument parsing, suite discovery in a temp folder, exit-code rules (enforced failure -> 1, pending invariant beyond --enforce -> 0, suite without fixture -> no_fixture and 0), offline guard throws on fetch. No network, no database.
FILES: package.json, vitest.eval.config.mts, server/src/features/match/eval/run.ts, server/src/features/match/eval/run.test.ts, server/src/features/match/eval/README.md

[P0] Metric functions and the gate table of strategy 2.6 (SM-1; strategy 2.6; MATCH 6.2)
CHANGE: New eval/metrics.ts, pure functions: recallAtK(ranked ids, labels, k, minGrade = 2); ndcgAtK (gain 2^grade - 1, log2 discount); weightedKappa (quadratic weights, for tiers and for judge against human grades); icc (two-way random, absolute agreement, single measure) over repeated scorer runs; spearman; precision and recall per class (for shown / related / not shown); tierFlipRate over runs; reliabilityCurve (mean AI score per estimate decile); shareEstimateGreatAiBelowPossible. New eval/gates.ts, data only, one entry per layer with the numbers of strategy 2.6: retrieval: Recall@200 hybrid >= recency-only + 15 points and no persona more than 5 points below its baseline; ranking: NDCG@10 and NDCG@20 no regression against fixtures/baselines.json (written by --write-baseline); estimate against AI: tier kappa >= 0.5 and "estimate Great, AI below Possible" under 5%; scorer: ICC >= 0.85 over 3 runs, tier flips under 5%, Spearman with human grades >= 0.6; taxonomy: category precision >= 95% on 300 labelled titles per market; skills: precision of "Not shown" >= 95%; language: zh-TW, zh-CN and cross-language subsets within 10% relative of the English subset; latency: feed p95 no worse than the stored baseline + 150 ms (live only). Rule in gates.ts: a metric computed from judge labels is reported untrusted until an audit file exists with judge-human weighted kappa >= 0.6.
ACCEPT: Every gate of strategy 2.6 exists as data with its threshold; a suite result is compared with its gate by one function used by run.ts; a gate whose layer has no suite yet prints not_built (it does not fail the command). Three suites ship now under eval/suites/: taxonomy.suite.ts (reads server/src/features/jobs/taxonomy/__fixtures__/labelledTitles.<market>.json by path when the files exist, else no_fixture, and calls matchTitle through seams.ts), ranking.suite.ts (NDCG@10 and @20 of the fit order against the constructed labels, through the getFits seam) and language.suite.ts (the same metric per subset en / zh-TW / zh-CN / cross).
TESTS: server/src/features/match/eval/metrics.test.ts: each metric against hand-computed examples (a perfect and a reversed ranking for NDCG and recall, a known 3x3 confusion table for kappa, identical runs give ICC 1, a monotone reversal gives Spearman -1); gates.test.ts: threshold comparison including the "+15 points" and "within 10% relative" rules.
FILES: server/src/features/match/eval/metrics.ts, server/src/features/match/eval/gates.ts, server/src/features/match/eval/suites/, server/src/features/match/eval/metrics.test.ts, server/src/features/match/eval/gates.test.ts

[P0] Synthetic personas, postings and constructed labels for both markets (SM-1; strategy 2.6; MATCH 6.1; D3)
CHANGE: New eval/fixtures/: personas.intl.json and personas.cn.json, 40 personas each: { id, market, locale, subset: en | zh-TW | zh-CN | cross, roleId (taxonomy id), level (one of the six SENIORITY_LEVELS), yearsExperience, skills[], location, payFloor, needsSponsorship (intl) or classYear and degree (cn), resumeMarkdown, recentTitles[] }. Coverage: the 15 largest role groups, three levels, career changers, new graduates; intl holds at least 8 Traditional Chinese personas and at least 4 cross-language cases (English resume against a Chinese or Japanese posting and the reverse); cn is Simplified Chinese plus at least 4 English-resume cases. postings.intl.json and postings.cn.json: at least 240 synthetic postings per market, written so every persona has a pool of at least 30 with intended grades 0-3, including the hard negatives the invariants need: same role two levels away, an internship, the same head noun in another discipline ("Java Backend Architect" against "Landscape Architect"), a posting that lists no skills and states no level, an implausible pay line, a posting located by country only. labels.constructed.intl.json / .cn.json: one graded label 0-3 per (persona, posting) recorded by the generator from how the posting was written; the file name and a "_kind": "constructed" key say these are not judge or human labels, and the report prints them as constructed. Every fixture file starts with "_synthetic": true. New eval/fixtures/build.ts (deterministic, seeded) and eval/fixtures/seed/ (hand-written role tables, skill sets, resume bullet banks in English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese) so the fixtures can be regenerated and reviewed. Nothing is copied from a job board, a provider response or a database row (repo rule: no copied production data; D3). Personas are test fixtures and never reach a user-facing surface.
ACCEPT: Counts and subsets as above; every persona has at least 5 postings graded 2 or 3 and at least 10 graded 0; running build.ts twice gives byte-identical files; grep finds no real employer name from the live index in the fixtures (the generator uses invented company names from seed/companies.json).
TESTS: server/src/features/match/eval/fixtures.test.ts: zod shape of every file, the counts and subset minimums, referential integrity of labels, determinism of build.ts (same seed, same hash).
FILES: server/src/features/match/eval/fixtures/, server/src/features/match/eval/fixtures.test.ts

[P0] The ten invariants as executable specs against the target contract (SM-1; strategy 2.2 (I1-I8) and 2.6; MATCH 6.3)
CHANGE: New eval/invariants.eval.ts and eval/seams.ts. invariants.eval.ts registers nothing at import: it exports registerInvariants({ enforce: 'M1' | 'M2' | 'M4' | 'all' }), which declares the ten vitest cases and marks those due after the enforced phase as pending (reported, not failing); a two-line entry eval/invariants.entry.eval.ts calls it with the runner's --enforce value. A later bundle calls the same function from a *.test.ts file to put the invariants of finished phases into npm test. seams.ts loads the functions under test by dynamic import through a variable path (so tsc does not resolve modules that do not exist yet) and throws SeamMissing("server/src/features/match/fit.ts#getFits") when a module or export is absent: a missing seam is a failing invariant, not a skipped one. Fakes come from the existing server/src/features/match/testkit.ts (createMemoryRepo, matchUser, matchJob, jobRecord, RESUME_MD) plus a counting fake scorer, a counting fake embeddings client and a counting fake planner. Each invariant declares the phase after which it must hold (due). The ten: INV-1 (due M1) a job with no listed skills and no stated level is never great and its confidence is low (getFits). INV-2 (due M1) changing filters.seniority, and any other FilterSet field that is not a logistics answer (taxonomyIds, titles, skills, companies), changes no field of the Fit for the same resume and job; changing location, pay or sponsorship answers changes the logistics dimension only. INV-3 (due M2) one user and one job read through every seam (feed card, job detail, Similar jobs, alert selection, Ready list fitsFor, Assistant storedFit and analyze_fit, extension chip, tailoring kit canonical fit) give the same score, tier and kind; the spec iterates a registry eval/seamRegistry.ts of { name, modulePath, read(userId, jobId) } so a seam that is missing fails by name. INV-4 (due M1) a senior resume against an internship is at most possible. INV-5 (due M1) matchTitle places "Java Backend Architect", "Lead AI Architect" and "Principal Architect - Machine Learning" outside the design category and "Landscape Architect" inside it. INV-6 (due M1; expected to pass already) a location entry with a country and no city filters by country: isCountryWideLocation and the locations predicate of features/feed/sql.ts, and locationCheck of features/match/preScore.ts. INV-7 (due M4) the keyword check reports PostgreSQL as related evidence for "relational databases" (item state related, via PostgreSQL) and lists no skill twice. INV-8 (due M1) pairwise: two candidates of equal true quality, one with an AI score and one with only the estimate, the AI-scored one never ranks below the other solely because it was scored (feed/ranking.ts fit input and recommendedRank). INV-9 (due M1; expected to pass already) "$60,000,000 an hour" is not sorted as pay (normalize payPlausible, feed/ranking.ts annualPay). INV-10 (due M1) on GoApply without the AI consent, getFit, a feed query and the precompute cron make zero calls on the counting fakes (scorer, embeddings, planner).
ACCEPT: On the base commit the handoff lists every invariant with pass or fail and the reason printed (expected failing at least: INV-1, INV-2, INV-3, INV-8, INV-10 by a missing seam or field, INV-7 by the missing state); none is skipped; the specs compile under npm run typecheck:server although the modules they target do not exist yet; after each phase merges the orchestrator runs --enforce for that phase.
TESTS: The specs are the tests. server/src/features/match/eval/seams.test.ts proves loadSeam returns an existing export and throws SeamMissing with the path for a missing one.
FILES: server/src/features/match/eval/invariants.eval.ts, server/src/features/match/eval/invariants.entry.eval.ts, server/src/features/match/eval/seams.ts, server/src/features/match/eval/seamRegistry.ts, server/src/features/match/eval/seams.test.ts

[P1] Live mode: frozen index snapshot, LLM judge with cache, recruiter audit and the dated report (SM-1; strategy 2.6, 7 item 18; MATCH 6.1, 6.5)
CHANGE: In run.ts and new eval/live/: --live runs only with EVAL_LIVE=1. snapshot.ts opens a read-only transaction (SET default_transaction_read_only = on) and writes, per persona, the pooled candidates (union of the top 50 of every retrieval variant under test) from the real index to eval/.snapshots/<yyyy-mm-dd>/ ; that folder is git-ignored by a new eval/.gitignore and is never committed. judge.ts: a fixed UMBRELA-style prompt (judgePrompt.ts, versioned) grading persona-posting pairs 0-3 with the model named by EVAL_JUDGE_MODEL; it refuses to run when that model equals the resolved scorer model (the judge must be a different, stronger model); outputs are cached by sha1(prompt version, persona id, posting content hash) so a re-run costs nothing. audit.ts: --export-audit writes a 10% sample as CSV for RoboHire and GoHire recruiters (persona summary, posting text, an empty grade column), --import-audit <csv> computes the quadratic-weighted kappa of judge against human and stores audit.json; while kappa is below 0.6 or no audit exists every judge-based metric prints untrusted. stability.ts: three scorer runs on 100 pairs for ICC and tier flips. report.ts writes report.md and report.json with the date, model ids, sample sizes and every gate. Only personas (synthetic) are sent to the judge and to embedding calls; no real user's resume or profile is read. Model cost goes through the existing usage log.
ACCEPT: Without EVAL_LIVE=1 or without --live nothing reads the database or the network; with both, a dated report is written under eval/.snapshots/ and nothing under version control changes; the report states which labels are constructed, judged or human and the sample size of each metric.
TESTS: server/src/features/match/eval/live/live.test.ts with a mocked LLM and a fake query function: judge prompt snapshot, cache hit on the second call, refusal when the judge model equals the scorer model, CSV export and import round trip with a known kappa, refusal without EVAL_LIVE. No network, no database.
FILES: server/src/features/match/eval/live/, server/src/features/match/eval/.gitignore, server/src/features/match/eval/run.ts
env: EVAL_LIVE: 1 allows "npm run eval:match -- --live" to read the database (read-only) and call models; anything else refuses (unset)
EVAL_JUDGE_MODEL: model id of the relevance judge for --live; must differ from the resolved LLM_MATCHING_MODEL (unset: --live refuses to judge)

bundles.title: Role taxonomy precision, enrichment override and backfill; data quality (SM-2, SM-10; query labels of SM-11)
items:
[P0] A head noun matches alone only when it is the whole title; a modifier lexicon decides the rest (SM-2; strategy 2.3 step 2; MATCH 4.5)
CHANGE: server/src/features/jobs/taxonomy/match.ts: replace the one-entry CONTEXT_REDIRECTS (lines 132-144, the "architect" case added by FIX-3) and its namedOutright pass in matchTitle (lines 192-211) with a general rule. (1) HEAD_NOUNS: architect, designer, developer, engineer, analyst, consultant, manager, specialist, technician and the Chinese equivalents 设计师, 工程师, 顾问, 专员, 经理, 分析师. A role phrase that is exactly one head noun (today: "architect" on node architect, "developer" on software_engineer, "consultant" on management_consultant) scores only when the level-stripped title (stripLevelWords) equals that word; inside a longer title it scores 0. For Chinese, a phrase equal to a head word scores only when the compact title equals it. (2) MODIFIER_LEXICON: for each head noun a map from modifier token to role id, built at module load from the taxonomy itself (every level-3 phrase of the form "<modifiers> <head noun>" contributes its modifier tokens to its role) and extended by an explicit list: java, backend, cloud, data, ai, ml, security, solutions, enterprise, 后端, 云, 数据 plus the existing SOFTWARE_CONTEXT words (lines 117-125) select software_architect for "architect". A title "<modifiers> <head noun>" whose modifiers select exactly one role scores 0.85 for it; when they select several, the role sharing most tokens wins and a tie gives no deterministic match (enrichment decides). (3) Review the 143 one-word English phrases of level-3 roles (for example pm, pt, np, ae, controller, trainer, buyer, trader, rater, doctor) and mark the ambiguous ones aloneOnly in a constant with a one-line reason each; list them in the handoff. server/src/features/jobs/taxonomy/taxonomy.v1.json: add the synonyms the rule needs (software_architect: solutions architect, cloud architect, data architect, security architect, ai architect, ml architect, microservices architect) and the mainland alias layer on existing nodes: 前端 / Web前端 / FE on the front-end role, 后端 / 服务端 on the back-end role, 管培生, 运营 families, 新媒体, 销售代表 variants on the nearest existing roles. No node id is added, removed or renamed (ids are stable; a new node is a taxonomy v2). Never copy a BOSS直聘 or 智联 category tree. matchTitle keeps its signature and returns the score it already returns (TitleMatch.score).
ACCEPT: Accepted when (SM-2): the architect cases pass: "Java Backend Architect", "Lead AI Architect", "Principal Architect - Machine Learning" and "Microservices Architect" resolve to software_architect (category software_engineering), "Landscape Architect", "Project Architect" and the bare title "Architect" to architect (category design). Added: "Senior Developer" still resolves to software_engineer (the head noun is the whole title after level words); "Sales Developer Representative" is not a software engineer; "UX Designer", "Interior Designer" and "Instructional Designer" land in three different roles; 前端开发工程师 and 服务端开发 resolve to the front-end and back-end roles; validateTaxonomy(taxonomy) returns no error.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/taxonomy/match.test.ts: one case per head noun in at least three disciplines, the Chinese head words, the tie rule, aloneOnly phrases; new taxonomy/idsFrozen.test.ts: validateTaxonomy returns no error and the set of node ids equals a frozen list (taxonomy.ts and taxonomy.test.ts are owned by the job-source bundle MKT-1C in this phase and are not edited here; the existing taxonomy.test.ts must stay green).
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/taxonomy/match.ts, server/src/features/jobs/taxonomy/taxonomy.v1.json, server/src/features/jobs/taxonomy/match.test.ts, server/src/features/jobs/taxonomy/idsFrozen.test.ts

[P0] Enrichment may override a deterministic role scored under 0.9; the match score is stored (SM-2; strategy 2.3 step 2; MATCH 4.5 points 2)
CHANGE: server/src/features/jobs/enrich/reconcile.ts, the block "Taxonomy: deterministic match wins; the model may only pick a candidate" (lines 399-411): today the model sets a role only when the row has none, so a wrong deterministic match is permanent. New rule: compute det = matchTitle(job.title, { limit: 1 })[0] inside reconcile (pure, no I/O). The model's taxonomyId is applied when it is one of the offered candidates AND (the row has no role, OR det is absent, OR det.score < 0.9). Deterministic wins only at det.score >= 0.9 (exact phrase, or the whole-title rule). update.titleMatchScore = det ? det.score : null is written on every reconcile, rules-only included, so the column says how strong the title evidence was whoever set the role. Report: add taxonomyOverridden: { from, to } | null to ReconcileReport and log it with the existing "model claims dropped" line in service.ts. needsLlm (reconcile.ts line 183): a row whose det.score < 0.9 needs the model even when deterministicCoverage is complete (reason weak_title_match). server/src/features/jobs/enrich/candidates.ts selectTaxonomyCandidates (line 73): always include the deterministic pick, and for a head-noun title every role the modifier lexicon lists for that head noun, inside MAX_TAXONOMY_CANDIDATES = 15. EnrichJobRecord / EnrichUpdate and repository.ts (loadJob select, toJobUpdateData line 106): add titleMatchScore. server/src/features/jobs/enrich/schema.ts (line 17): ENRICH_VERSION 1 -> 2, so live rows are re-enriched by the existing jobs-maintain step (ingest/maintain.ts buildStaleEnrichSql) inside the existing daily enrichment budget; rows keep serving their old role until their turn.
ACCEPT: A row titled "Java Backend Architect" stored under architect with a deterministic score below 0.9 and a model pick software_architect from the candidates ends under software_architect with taxonomyIds [category, group, role] and report.taxonomyOverridden set; a title that matches a role phrase exactly keeps its deterministic role even when the model disagrees; a model id outside the candidates is still rejected (taxonomyRejected); a rules-only finish still writes titleMatchScore.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/enrich/reconcile.test.ts (override, exact-match keep, rejected id, rules-only write), candidates.test.ts (deterministic pick and lexicon roles always offered), repository.test.ts (column written), service.test.ts (weak title triggers the model call; the call is a mocked EnrichLlm).
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/enrich/reconcile.ts, server/src/features/jobs/enrich/candidates.ts, server/src/features/jobs/enrich/repository.ts, server/src/features/jobs/enrich/schema.ts, server/src/features/jobs/enrich/service.ts and their tests

[P0] Labelled title set (300 per market) and the 95% category-precision gate (SM-2; strategy 2.6 taxonomy gate; MATCH 4.5 point 5)
CHANGE: New server/src/features/jobs/taxonomy/__fixtures__/labelledTitles.intl.json and labelledTitles.cn.json: 300 titles each as { title, categoryId, roleId | null, note? }, written by the engineer from the role tree and common posting vocabulary (not copied from a job board): every head noun of the previous item in several disciplines, level words, bracketed notes, tech spellings (C++, .NET, Node.js); intl includes at least 40 Traditional Chinese titles (工程師, 專員, 儲備幹部; they are folded by normalize/zhVariants.ts foldTwToCn before matching) and 20 mixed-language titles; cn includes 校招 / 实习 / 管培生 titles and mainland role vocabulary. The label is the category a recruiter would file the title under; a title that should stay unknown has categoryId null. New taxonomy/precision.test.ts computes category-level precision (correct category among titles that got a deterministic category) and asserts >= 0.95 per market, and prints the misses. The harness of MKT-1D ships a taxonomy suite that reads these two files by path when they exist; this bundle does not edit the harness and exports no test helper from production code.
ACCEPT: Accepted when (SM-2): >= 95% category precision on the labelled set, per market; the architect cases pass. Added: every head-noun case in the set is correct; a title labelled unknown is not forced into a category.

[P0] Estimate v2 (a): the level and the role come from the resume and profile, never from filter chips (SM-3; strategy M-8, 2.2 I3, 2.4; MATCH 3.3, 4.4 points 1-2)
CHANGE: server/src/features/match/context.ts buildMatchUser (lines 153-191) and server/src/features/match/preScore.ts. The level already comes from the resume (userLevel, resumeSeniority; FIX-3). The role still comes from the saved search: userTargets() (preScore.ts lines 307-314) reads user.targetTaxonomyIds and targetTitles, which buildMatchUser fills from filters.taxonomyIds and filters.titles (context.ts lines 172-173), so a job inside the role filter scores 1.0 by construction and editing the Role chips moves every fit. With no role evidence the title_level component is not stated and takes its prior (next item) with the confidence reason no_role_evidence; the saved search is not read for it. targetTaxonomyIds, targetTitles and targetSeniority stay on MatchUser only as what the AI scorer is told the person is looking for (MatchService.ts line 543) and are documented as not inputs of the estimate. The level factor keeps seniorityFactor (0 levels apart 1, one 0.7, two 0.3, more 0, unknown 0.8) with the resume level; with no resume and no experience the level comes from RAProfile.seekerType when set (SEEKER_TYPES in features/onboarding/contract.ts line 248: student and recent_graduate -> intern_newgrad; experienced and career_change give no level), and confidence is low. Stated eligibility stays as it is: a degree the user does not meet and, on GoApply, a stated 届别 the user is not in, each halve the factor; 届别 only from a quoted tag (classYearsFromTags), school tier never an input, an age limit in a posting is never read.
ACCEPT: Accepted when (SM-3): Level chips do not move any fit. Added (I3): for the same resume, profile and job, changing filters.seniority, filters.taxonomyIds, filters.titles, filters.skills or filters.companies changes no field of the result; changing only the location, pay or sponsorship answers changes the logistics dimension and the total, nothing else; a senior resume against an internship is at most possible (levelGap >= 2 cap kept); a resume whose two recent titles are "Teacher" gets a low title_level for a "Data Analyst" job even when the saved search targets data analysts.

[P0] Estimate v2 (b): priors instead of renormalisation, hard skills only, the logistics rule, coverage and confidence (SM-3; strategy M-8, 2.2 I4, 2.4; MATCH 4.4 points 3-6)
CHANGE: server/src/features/match/preScore.ts and config.ts. (1) Priors. combineDimensions (lines 264-274) renormalises over the scored components; replace it for the estimate with combineWithPriors(dimensions, priors): a not-stated component contributes its prior at its FULL weight (35/30/15/10/10 from getMatchWeights), so total = sum(weight x (score or prior)) / 100. Starting priors (strategy 2.4, from 202 stored scorer-v3 rows): title_level 44, skills 39, industry 24, career_path 45; logistics has no figure in the strategy, use 50 as a neutral starting value (see notes). New getMatchPriors(brand, env) in config.ts reads MATCH_PRIORS / CN_MATCH_PRIORS through brandEnv with the validation style of getMatchWeights (lines 49-61). The honesty caps of preScoreLimit (lines 586-601) stay as a second guard; the null rule stays: with neither role nor skills comparable the score is null, never 0. Worked check that must hold: a posting with no skills, a perfect title match (100) and logistics really met (100) gives (35x100 + 30x39 + 15x24 + 10x100 + 10x45) / 100 = 64.8, so at most 65 and never great. (2) Hard skills only. jobSkillList (lines 399-405) merges skillsDetail and skills; restrict numerator and denominator of skillsDimension (lines 422-432) to entries whose kind is not soft (skillsDetail.kind; a skill with no detail entry counts as hard), required weighted 1 and preferred 0.5: score = 100 x (sum of weights shown) / (sum of weights listed, over at most the first 10 by required-first order). Soft skills stay visible in splitSkills output for display under a separate softSkills list and never enter the number. (3) Logistics. logisticsDimension (lines 546-561): not_met stays a real penalty. A check that is met only because the user's own saved search makes that field a hard filter carries no information: location is filter-guaranteed when user.locations, user.workModels or user.country is set; pay when user.salaryMin is set; visa when needsSponsorship is true. When every stated check is met and each of them is filter-guaranteed, the dimension contributes the logistics prior instead of 100 and its evidence carries ref logistics_by_your_filters; any not_met gives 100 x met / stated as today. The rule depends only on the user and the job, never on the surface the job was opened from, so every surface gets the same number. (4) Coverage and confidence on PreScoreResult: coverage = sum of weights of components with stated evidence on BOTH sides / 100 (career_path never counts for an estimate; a filter-guaranteed logistics counts as not backed); postingCoverage = share of weight the POSTING states (role placed 35, skills listed 30, employer industry known 15, location or pay stated 10; career_path is resume-side and is excluded from the denominator of 90). confidence: high at coverage >= 0.75, medium from 0.5 to under 0.75, low below 0.5; and whenever postingCoverage < 0.6 the confidence is low and the total is capped at tiers.great - 1 (I4). confidenceReason: one of no_skills_listed | no_level_stated | no_role_evidence | no_resume | few_details, the first that applies. server/src/features/match/contract.ts: add coverage: number, confidence: 'high' | 'medium' | 'low', confidenceReason: string | null to PreScoreResult and MatchFitView (additive; kind keeps the wire value 'pre' for an estimate so the published extension and the web keep working), and softSkills: string[] to MatchFitView.skills.
ACCEPT: Accepted when (SM-3): a no-skills job is never Great. Added: the worked example gives 65 or less; a posting that states less than 60% of the rubric weight is never great and has confidence low (I4); a job listing only soft skills ("communication", "attention to detail") has a not-stated skills component; preferred skills count half; with location, pay and visa all met only through the saved search the logistics dimension equals the prior and the evidence says so; MATCH_PRIORS={"skills":"x"} keeps the defaults.
TESTS: server/src/features/match/preScore.test.ts: the worked example; priors per component; hard, soft, required and preferred weighting; the three logistics cases (filter-guaranteed, really met without a filter, not met); coverage and confidence thresholds at 0.49 / 0.5 / 0.74 / 0.75 and the postingCoverage 0.6 rule; config tests for getMatchPriors (brand fallback, malformed input).
FILES: server/src/features/match/preScore.ts, server/src/features/match/config.ts, server/src/features/match/contract.ts, server/src/features/match/preScore.test.ts

[P0] The fit contract: match/fit.ts with getFit, getFits and getVariantFit; job content hash and rubric version in the key; versions never silently miss (SM-5; strategy 2.2 (I1, I2, I5, I7, I8); MATCH 4.3)

Tier hysteresis (I5): when a stored row is recomputed without a model call (logistics or weights changed, lines 500-511) the stored tier changes only if the new total is at least 3 points past the threshold it crosses; a new model result takes its own tier. preScoreMany (lines 647-679) and scoreJob become thin callers of the same internals so there is one implementation; listAiScores (repo.ts line 53) drops the promptVersion filter and returns generatedAt, modelUsed, promptVersion, jobContentHash. items:

CHANGE: No production code changes in this item. Read rules A1-A12 and the G table of section 5.3. The Alipay path "must keep working exactly as it does": every change in this bundle is additive and lives in server/src/platform/billing/rails/alipayWorker.ts and server/src/platform/billing/origins.ts only. server/src/platform/billing/fulfilPass.ts is NOT edited at all (not a line, not a comment); the callback route in server/src/roboapply/routes/billing.ts (lines 186-199) and handleAlipayCallback in RoboApplyBillingService.ts (lines 542-571) are not edited; the AlipayOrder table is not changed; the fulfilPass signature { outTradeNo, channel, paidAmountMinor, transactionId } and the rail registration in rails/index.ts (ensureDefaultRails) keep their shape (this bundle may only add one log call there, item 2). The characterisation tests the parity wave wrote for A1-A12 (in RoboApplyBillingService.alipay.test.ts, rails/rails.test.ts, fulfilPass.test.ts and server/src/roboapply/routes/billing.test.ts) stay green and UNEDITED: not renamed, not re-ordered, no assertion touched. New assertions go in the two new test files of this bundle. The only pre-existing assertions that may change are ones that are not A-tests (their names do not start with 'A<number> ') and pin a value AL-3 changes on purpose. In rails/rails.test.ts as the parity wave left it (docs/jobright-clone/orch/handoffs-par/PAR-6.md, findings 1 and 2) there are three: the GAORDER_ prefix regex in 'creates a whole-yuan order with the GoApply callback, return URL and collecting entity' (becomes RAORDER_); the test 'creates the order without an entity: the body is the subject alone and every other field is unchanged' (it asserts that body equals the subject and that both requests have the same key list; it becomes: no body key, every other key and value unchanged); and the last assertion of the test 'never borrows another brand's entity: …' (body equals the subject; it becomes: no body key). List every such edit, with file, test name and line, in the handoff. The A-tests were written against the code as it is and several are strict; read them before coding: 'A5 the body: …' pins the exact key set WITH an entity configured (body stays in that set: G6 drops it only when no entity is set); the A6 tests build the rail on a database object that throws on every property and still expect a callback with a valid secret to resolve (item 4 says what that means for the amount tolerance); 'A2 400 / 40004 …' sends total_amount=1.00; 'A10 …' compares the history rows with toEqual. If a change of this bundle makes a test named 'A<number> …' fail, the change is wrong: rework it; never edit, skip or rename the test. If you believe a rule of the G table cannot be met without editing one, stop and write a Request to the orchestrator that names the test. No answer code of rule A2 is added, removed or renumbered.
ACCEPT: Run before starting and after finishing: npx vitest run server/src/roboapply/services/RoboApplyBillingService.alipay.test.ts server/src/platform/billing server/src/roboapply/routes/billing.test.ts. Both runs pass; git diff shows no change in fulfilPass.ts, routes/billing.ts, RoboApplyBillingService.ts or any A1-A12 test body; the handoff names each edited pre-existing assertion.

[P0] Notify URL on GoApply's own host, another host only by explicit override; host logged at startup (AL-3 part 1; MARKET_STRATEGY 5.3 G8, C1)
CHANGE: server/src/platform/billing/origins.ts: add alipayNotifyOrigin(brand, env). GoApply (brand.market === 'cn'): CN_ALIPAY_NOTIFY_ORIGIN when it parses as an https origin (an invalid value is ignored and logged) -> CN_BACKEND_URL (the brand-own read: brandOwnEnv(brand, 'BACKEND_URL', env) after the parity wave; it must never resolve to the shared BACKEND_URL) -> brand.canonicalOrigin (https://www.goapply.top, today's behaviour). It NEVER falls back to BACKEND_URL or to www.roboapply.io: during the M-18 window that host runs main, whose handler has no amount check and would mis-activate or not find the order. RoboApply (legacy orders only, no new purchase) keeps callbackOrigin unchanged (lines 25-27). server/src/platform/billing/rails/alipayWorker.ts notify_url (today line 123) uses alipayNotifyOrigin; return_url (line 124) stays on appOrigin. Add logAlipayNotifyHostOnce(env): one info line per process with the HOST ONLY of the resolved GoApply notify origin and which variable decided it (never the cb secret, never a full URL with query); call it from ensureDefaultRails in rails/index.ts when the alipay rail is registered.

Added: CN_BACKEND_URL=https://api.goapply.example gives that host with no double slash; CN_ALIPAY_NOTIFY_ORIGIN wins over CN_BACKEND_URL; BACKEND_URL=https://www.roboapply.io alone changes nothing for GoApply; an http or malformed override is ignored and logged; the startup line prints the host and no secret; return_url is on the GoApply app origin; the cb query parameter is still URL-encoded (rule A5).

[P0] Request body back to production's shape: RAORDER_ for both brands, body only with an entity, package_id mode (AL-3 part 2; MARKET_STRATEGY 5.3 G6, G7, G10; PAY A2, R9-R11)
CHANGE: server/src/platform/billing/rails/alipayWorker.ts. G7: newOutTradeNo (today lines 68-72) uses the prefix RAORDER for both brands (the brand is in AlipayOrder.brand); keep the timestamp, user and random parts and fix the comment on line 67. G6: the payload (lines 107-125) sends body only when a collecting entity is configured ('<subject> · <entity>', at most 200 characters); without an entity the key is absent, as in production (today line 111 always sends it). G10: package_data (lines 117-122) keeps package_id = the plan key by default; CN_ALIPAY_PACKAGE_ID_MODE=legacy sends package_id 'starter' and keeps the plan key in package_name (the fallback if the worker validates the id; the supervised order of AL-8 decides); package_type '1' and package_price as a string are unchanged. Everything else of rule A5 is untouched: endpoint default https://worker.gohire.top/payment/payment/create, pay_channel 'alipay', platform 'gohire' unless CN_ALIPAY_PLATFORM / ROBOAPPLY_ALIPAY_PLATFORM, whole-yuan numeric total_amount, user_name / user_email / user_id.

Added: with no entity the set of keys sent is exactly out_trade_no, total_amount, subject, pay_channel, user_name, user_email, user_id, platform, package_data, notify_url, return_url; out_trade_no matches /^RAORDER_\d{14}_.{1,8}_[0-9a-f]{10}$/ on both brands (the middle part is the first 8 characters of the user id, which may contain an underscore); with CN_ALIPAY_PACKAGE_ID_MODE=legacy package_id is 'starter' and package_name the plan key; a stored order row still has tier 'ra_<planKey>' and brand 'goapply'.
TESTS: server/src/platform/billing/rails/alipayWorker.wire.test.ts (new; fetch is a vi.fn, the database is createFakePrisma): the exact key set compared with a production-shape fixture taken from PAYMENTS_AUDIT A2; prefix; body present only with CN_PAYMENT_COLLECTING_ENTITY; both package modes. server/src/platform/billing/rails/rails.test.ts: the three assertions named in item 1 that are not A-tests are adapted (the prefix regex becomes RAORDER_; the two no-entity assertions expect no body key and otherwise the same keys and values); every test named 'A5 …' passes unedited.
FILES: server/src/platform/billing/rails/alipayWorker.ts, rails/alipayWorker.wire.test.ts, rails/rails.test.ts

[P0] Callback amount tolerance: yuan or fen accepted, an implausible value treated as not stated, a real mismatch still refused (AL-4 part 1; MARKET_STRATEGY 5.3 G9; PAY R8)
CHANGE: server/src/platform/billing/rails/alipayWorker.ts verifyCallback (today lines 167-183; the amount is parsed on lines 179-180 as yuan only). Order of work, which keeps rule A6 and the A6 tests as the parity wave wrote them: (1) the secret check exactly as today, before any database access; (2) the parameter check (pay_status, out_trade_no); (3) parse total_amount WITHOUT the database: absent -> null; not well-formed (letters, negative, more than two decimals, empty string) -> null (not stated) with one warn log carrying the order number and the raw value's length, not the value; well-formed (/^\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$/, greater than zero) but above ¥1,000,000 -> null (implausible: not stated) with the same warn log; otherwise the yuan reading round(value x 100), exactly as today. (4) The order is read ONLY when the value can be a fen amount: it is written without a decimal point and is an integer multiple of 100 (a whole-yuan price in fen always is: 1200, 3900, 9900; '39.00', '39' and the JSON number 39 never are). In that one case read the order once, db.alipayOrder.findUnique({ where: { outTradeNo }, select: { amount, amountMinor } }) through the rail's own getDb, with expected = amountMinor ?? round(amount x 100): value x 100 equals expected (it was yuan) -> expected; value equals expected (it was fen: exactly 100 times the expected yuan, e.g. 3900 for ¥39) -> expected, with one info log 'total_amount read as fen'; anything else -> the yuan reading unchanged, so fulfilPass answers amount_mismatch and the route answers 400 / 40004 as today. No order row, or ANY error while reading it (a database failure included) -> the yuan reading, as today: the read sits in try / catch and never makes verifyCallback throw (fulfilPass then answers not_found / 40002 for an unknown order, as today). Why so narrow: the parity wave's tests 'A6 the secret may arrive as ?cb=, as a JSON body field or as the x-alipay-callback-secret header' and 'A6 the trade facts the callback reads: status mapping, amount in fen, the provider trade number' (rails/rails.test.ts) build the rail with a getDb whose object throws on every property and expect a callback with a valid secret and total_amount '39.00', '39', 39 or none to resolve with today's values; they stay unedited, so a callback that does not need the order must not touch the database. Not changed here (PAR-6 handoff, finding 4): a replay of an already paid order that states a genuinely different amount still answers 40004, because fulfilPass checks the amount before the claim; no rule of the G table changes that and fulfilPass.ts is not edited. The function still returns { outTradeNo, status, paidAmountMinor, transactionId }; fulfilPass and its signature are not touched.
ACCEPT: (section 9, AL-4) total_amount=3900 and 39.00 both fulfil a ¥39 order; 40.00 refuses. Added: 39 fulfils; 4000 refuses (40004, order stays pending); "abc" and "-39" fulfil as not stated and are logged; a missing total_amount fulfils as today; an unknown order number still answers 40002; a wrong cb is refused before the order is read (the fake database records zero reads); a valid callback with total_amount 39.00, 39 or none makes zero database reads at the rail and one with 3900 makes exactly one; when that one read throws, the yuan reading is returned and nothing else throws; a value above ¥1,000,000 is treated as not stated and logged; every test named 'A6 …' and 'A2 …' passes unedited.
TESTS: server/src/platform/billing/rails/alipayWorker.callback.test.ts (new; createFakePrisma seeded with one pending order of 3900 fen): the table above at the rail level, the read counts (zero, zero, zero, one) and a getDb that throws for the 3900 case; server/src/roboapply/services/RoboApplyBillingService.alipay.test.ts: NEW cases only, appended in a new describe block, for the route answers (200 code 0 for 3900 and 39.00; 400 / 40004 for 40.00).
FILES: server/src/platform/billing/rails/alipayWorker.ts, rails/alipayWorker.callback.test.ts, server/src/roboapply/services/RoboApplyBillingService.alipay.test.ts

[P0] Secret-less callbacks only for orders created before the cut-over instant, and only for 7 days after it (AL-4 part 2; MARKET_STRATEGY 5.3 G4, C7)
CHANGE: server/src/platform/billing/rails/alipayWorker.ts verifyCallback. Today: no secret configured -> not_configured (503 / 50003); a missing or wrong cb with a secret configured -> bad_secret (403 / 40003). Keep both. Add one path: when a secret IS configured and the callback carries NO cb at all (not in the query, the body or the x-alipay-callback-secret header) and ALIPAY_SECRETLESS_UNTIL parses as an ISO instant T: accept the callback only if now < T + 7 days AND the order exists AND order.createdAt < T, evaluated in that order so the database is opened only inside a live window (with the variable unset or unparseable, or once T + 7 days has passed, a callback without cb is refused without any database access: the parity wave's test 'A6 a wrong, missing or near-miss cb is refused as bad_secret without opening the database' pins that and stays unedited); log one warn line with the order number. In every other case answer bad_secret as today. A callback that carries a cb which does not match is ALWAYS refused, before any database access, whatever the variable says (constant-time comparison unchanged, rule A6). With the variable unset, empty or unparseable nothing changes. Put the two constants (7 days) next to the function with a comment that the window exists for orders production created before the cut-over if production ran without a secret (cut-over checklist step 1).
ACCEPT: (section 9, AL-4) A no-cb callback fulfils only an order older than ALIPAY_SECRETLESS_UNTIL, and none once 7 days have passed. Added: an order created one second after T is refused (403 / 40003); a wrong cb is refused even inside the window and without a database read; with no secret configured the answer is still 503 / 50003; with the variable unset every A1-A12 test passes unedited.
TESTS: server/src/platform/billing/rails/alipayWorker.callback.test.ts (clock injected through deps.now: before T + 7 d, after it, order older and newer than T, wrong cb, unset variable); RoboApplyBillingService.alipay.test.ts: one new route-level case in the new describe block.
FILES: server/src/platform/billing/rails/alipayWorker.ts, rails/alipayWorker.callback.test.ts, server/src/roboapply/services/RoboApplyBillingService.alipay.test.ts
env: CN_ALIPAY_NOTIFY_ORIGIN: https origin that receives GoApply Alipay notifies; set it to another host only when that host runs this code on the same database (default unset -> CN_BACKEND_URL -> https://www.goapply.top)
ALIPAY_SECRETLESS_UNTIL: ISO instant; a callback without cb is accepted only for orders created before it and only until 7 days after it (default unset = never)
CN_ALIPAY_PACKAGE_ID_MODE: legacy sends package_id starter and the plan key in package_name (default unset = the plan key as package_id)
