bundles.title: Self-service withdrawal endpoints (signed in and on the public cancel page) and consent retention after account deletion (server)
items:
[P0] Signed-in withdrawal: quote, then confirm (ST-9 server; MARKET_STRATEGY 4.4 "Statutory withdrawal", M-21, Directive (EU) 2023/2673). The control is MKT-4C.
CHANGE: server/src/features/credits/routes.ts createCreditsRouter: GET /withdrawal and POST /withdrawal (seeker auth, billingRoute). service.ts: CreditsAreaService.withdrawalQuote(userId, brand) and withdraw(userId, brand, body), thin calls to withdrawalQuote and withdrawPurchase of server/src/platform/billing/stripeRefunds.ts (MKT-2D; import by file path or from the billing index, which exports them since M2), with actor 'self'; GoApply always answers available false (the mainland rails have no refund call; its published rule is on /pricing). POST is rate-limited to 3 an hour per user (this.d.rateLimit) and invalidates entitlements. The existing admin refundQuote (today lines 747-854) passes the subscription's period bounds to computeRefund so the admin quote shows the pro-rata amount too (read the Stripe subscription with stripePeriod when the latest charge is a subscription invoice). contract.ts: WithdrawBodySchema and the two response types. Contract (identical in MKT-4C): GET /api/v1/roboapply/credits/withdrawal -> { available: boolean, purchase: { source: 'stripe', id: string, planKey: string, chargedAt: string, amountMinor: number, currency: string } | null, quote: { rule: 'withdrawal_14d' | 'withdrawal_14d_prorata', refundMinor: number, currency: string, deadline: string, prorata: { usedDays: number, periodDays: number } | null, endsAccess: true, region: 'eu' | 'uk' | 'tw' } | null }. POST /api/v1/roboapply/credits/withdrawal { purchaseId: string, confirm: true } -> { status: 'withdrawn', refundMinor: number, currency: string, accessEnded: true }; errors 409 withdrawal_not_available, 429 rate_limited, 503 rail_not_configured, 502 payment_provider_error. The quote is available for 14 days after each purchase of a buyer whose billing country is in the EU, the EEA, the UK or Taiwan, with or without the waiver (the amount differs), and never for a renewal.
ACCEPT: (section 9) A German subscriber who ticked the waiver and withdraws on day 5 of 30 is quoted 25/30 of the price, the subscription is cancelled at once and Pro ends. Add POST /preview { token }: validates the emailed single-use token exactly as confirm does (kind billing_cancel, brand, not consumed, not expired) WITHOUT consuming it, and answers what the link can do. Extend POST /confirm with an optional withdraw: true: the token is claimed first as today; with withdraw the service runs withdrawPurchase for the quoted purchase (actor 'public_link') instead of the period-end cancel; if the withdrawal is not available any more it falls back to the ordinary cancel and says so in the answer; a provider failure releases the token as today (lines 583-591). [P1] The renewal acknowledgement outlives the account: kept until the later of 3 years after consent and 1 year after the subscription ends (ST-9 "consent retention"; MARKET_STRATEGY 4.4 "Renewal", California AB 2863)
CHANGE: Today the records (SeekerConsentRecord of type auto_renew_ack, withdrawal_waiver, cn_pay_terms_ack) are deleted with the account: SeekerAccountPurgeService.ts line 221 deletes the User and the cascade removes them 30 days after a deletion request, which can be less than the law's period. New server/src/platform/billing/consentArchive.ts: billingConsentRetainUntil(consentedAt, subscriptionEndedAt) = the later of consentedAt + 3 years and (subscriptionEndedAt ?? now) + 1 year; archiveBillingConsents(db, userId, now): for each billing consent record of the user's seeker profile insert one RABillingConsentArchive row (schema below) with userId, emailHash = sha256 of the lower-cased email, brand, consentType, proseHash, proseVersion, consentedAt = the record's createdAt, subscriptionEndedAt = the subscription's canceledAt or currentPeriodEnd when it is in the past, stripeCustomerId and retainUntil; rows whose retainUntil is already in the past are not written; IP address and user agent are NOT copied (the hash of the sentence is the proof). server/src/roboapply/services/SeekerAccountPurgeService.ts: call archiveBillingConsents inside the purge, before the delete of line 221, in a way that a repeated purge run does not duplicate rows (skip when rows for that userId exist). server/src/features/compliance/retention.ts: the rule billing_consent_records (lines 437-442) now says the records are kept for that period even after the account is deleted, and a new rule billing_consent_archive deletes archive rows whose retainUntil has passed (enforcedBy 'compliance-daily', batched, brand-scoped like its neighbours; add the delegate to RetentionDb) with its English and Chinese labels next to the others (lines 490-525). BILLING_CONSENT_KEEP (line 224) stays 36 months as the minimum.
ACCEPT: A subscriber who consented 30 months ago and deletes the account today keeps an archive row until month 42 (one year after the end); one who consented 4 years ago and whose subscription ended 2 years ago leaves no row; the archive row holds no IP, no user agent and no email in clear; the daily retention run deletes a row the day after its retainUntil and not before; running the purge twice writes the rows once; the published retention schedule lists the new rule in English and Chinese.
TESTS: server/src/platform/billing/consentArchive.test.ts (new: the date rule and the mapping); server/src/roboapply/services/SeekerAccountPurgeService.consent.test.ts (new: archive written before deletion, idempotent; the Prisma client is mocked as in the existing purge tests); server/src/features/compliance/retention.test.ts (the new rule's sweep; the schedule text; the existing "kept minimum" assertions at lines 476-477 still hold).
FILES: server/src/platform/billing/consentArchive.ts, consentArchive.test.ts, server/src/roboapply/services/SeekerAccountPurgeService.ts, SeekerAccountPurgeService.consent.test.ts, server/src/features/compliance/retention.ts, retention.test.ts
schema:
model RABillingConsentArchive (new, server/prisma/schema/ra-credits.prisma; additive; no relation fields):
/// Checkout acknowledgements kept after the account is deleted (California AB 2863: the later of 3 years after
/// consent and 1 year after the subscription ends). Written by the account purge, removed by compliance-daily. ST-9.
model RABillingConsentArchive {
  id                  String    @id @default(cuid())
  /// The deleted account's user id (no FK) and sha256 of its lower-cased email.
  userId              String
  emailHash           String
  brand               String
  consentType         String    // 'auto_renew_ack' | 'withdrawal_waiver' | 'cn_pay_terms_ack'
  proseHash           String?
  proseVersion        String?
  consentedAt         DateTime
  subscriptionEndedAt DateTime?
  stripeCustomerId    String?
  retainUntil         DateTime
  createdAt           DateTime  @default(now())

  @@index([retainUntil])
  @@index([emailHash])
  @@index([userId])
}
Everything above is delivered by MKT-0 in phase M0 (see its schema array for the exact Prisma text); this bundle never edits *.prisma and never runs a push.

CHANGE: The Alipay rail has no refund call: staff return the money in the Alipay (or WeChat Pay) merchant console, then record it. adminRoutes.ts: GET /cn-orders?userId= (completed ra_ orders of a user with a refunded marker) and POST /cn-orders/:orderId/refund. bundles.title: Enrichment v3: canonical skill ids at write time, honest keywords, requirements extracted once per posting (SM-6 write path, SM-8 job side)
items:
[P0] Skills are written with canonical ids; provider fields first; hard and soft kept apart (SM-6; strategy 1.5 row "Provider fields first", 2.3 step 5; MATCH 4.6 write path)
CHANGE: server/src/features/jobs/enrich/reconcile.ts, the skills block (lines 352-376): today skills are free lower-case strings, skillsDetail carries kind and required, and RAJob.skills mixes hard and soft. New, after the grounded-skill filter (skillGrounded): map every skill through canonicalizeMany of server/src/features/skills (MKT-2G) with the dependencies wired here for the first time: embed = embedTexts(brand, texts, { purpose: 'skill', carriesUserData: false }) of server/src/platform/embeddings (MKT-2H), nearest = the RASkill neighbour query, create = insert of an unreviewed skill; when the embeddings client is unavailable only the exact-alias step runs. Order of sources: the provider's own skill field first (job.skills from ingest), then the model's list, so the model fills only what the provider did not give. Results: skillsDetail items gain skillId (null when no canonical skill was found) and keep skill (display string), kind (the vocabulary's kind wins over the model's when the skill is reviewed) and required; update.skillIds = the distinct ids of hard and certification skills, required first, at most 25; update.skills stays the display strings for the existing GIN filter and typeahead; a skill whose canonical kind is soft stays in skillsDetail (shown) and is left out of skillIds (never scored). reconcile stays a pure function: the canonical mapping is computed in enrich/service.ts before reconcile is called and passed in as a map term -> { skillId, kind, status }. EnrichUpdate, EnrichJobRecord and repository.ts toJobUpdateData: add skillIds. The mention counter of each mapped skill is increased by one (repo call batched per job) so the review list of the skills CLI is ordered by real frequency.
ACCEPT: A posting whose model output lists "postgres", "PostgreSQL" and "communication" ends with one PostgreSQL entry carrying skillId postgresql in skillsDetail, skillIds containing postgresql and not the soft skill, and both display strings still searchable in RAJob.skills; a skill the vocabulary does not know is stored as an unreviewed skill and shown, and is absent from every score; with no embedding key the alias path still fills ids; no skill is stored that the posting does not name (skillGrounded unchanged).
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/enrich/reconcile.test.ts (ids, kinds, required-first order, soft excluded, cap 25), service.test.ts (canonicalizeMany called once per job with a fake vocabulary, embeddings unavailable path), repository.test.ts (skillIds written). All model and embedding calls are fakes.
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/enrich/reconcile.ts, service.ts, repository.ts and their tests

[P0] Keywords: only concrete, canonical terms; generic words and loose phrases are dropped at the source (SM-6; MATCH 3.2 enrichment row, 4.6 (generic words and TF-IDF phrases without a canonical id are dropped at the source))
CHANGE: server/src/features/jobs/enrich/keywords.ts buildKeywords (line 219): the list is skills first, then TF-IDF terms of the posting's own sentences, which produces phrases such as "shared backend systems" that the keyword check then reports as missing. New rule: a keyword is kept only when it is (a) a skill of the posting with a canonical id whose kind is hard or certification, importance high when required and medium when preferred, or (b) a TF-IDF term (tfidfTerms, line 155) that the vocabulary resolves to a reviewed hard or certification skill (idOf through the synchronous snapshot; no embedding call here), importance low. Everything else is dropped: generic words ("software engineering", "communication"), soft skills, phrases with no canonical id. Extend the stop lists the same way for Chinese (岗位职责, 任职要求, 优先, 熟悉, 负责, 相关经验 and the like) so they never reach step (b). JobKeyword gains skillId. The RAKeywordExtraction row is rewritten whenever a job is re-enriched (writeKeywords in service.ts).
ACCEPT: The keyword list of the "Senior Backend Engineer" fixture contains its tools and methods (each with a skillId) and none of "communication", "shared backend systems", "fast-paced"; a Chinese posting fixture yields its tools and certificates and no boilerplate words; no keyword appears twice under two spellings.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/enrich/keywords.test.ts with a fixture vocabulary: kept and dropped terms in English and Chinese, importance mapping, de-duplication by id.
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/enrich/keywords.ts, keywords.test.ts, service.ts

[P0] Requirements are extracted once per posting and stored on the job (SM-8; strategy 2.3 step 7 (requirements extracted once per job); MATCH 4.8)
CHANGE: server/src/features/jobs/enrich/schema.ts EnrichLlmOutputSchema: add requirements: array of { kind: skill | experience | education | domain | scope, text, importance: must | preferred }, parsed leniently (bad items dropped), at most ENRICH_REQUIREMENTS_MAX = 12. enrich/agent.ts buildEnrichMessages (line 133): ask for the posting's requirement lines copied verbatim (each at most 240 characters), the ones marked required, minimum or must as must and the rest as preferred; no paraphrase, no merged lines, nothing about location, pay or visa (those are logistics and are computed elsewhere). reconcile.ts: keep an item only when its text is a verbatim substring of the posting after normalizeForQuote (quotes.ts), drop duplicates by normalised text, assign ids r1…rN in posting order, and return update.requirements = { v: 1, contentHash: jobContentHash(job) (server/src/features/match/jobHash.ts), model, extractedAt, items } using the JobRequirement type of server/src/features/match/contract.ts. A rules-only finish writes no requirements (null): the scorer of MKT-4G then extracts them in its own call and stores them, first writer wins. A re-enrichment replaces the list only when the content hash changed. repository.ts: write the column. On GoApply: 届别 and 学历 lines are requirements of kind education like any other and are quoted; an age limit stated in a posting is NOT extracted as a requirement and is never an input of any score or filter; it is recorded as a market tag { tag: 'age_limit_stated', evidenceQuote } beside the other quoted tags so the card code can flag the posting (strategy 2.5 row "Eligibility").
ACCEPT: A posting with "5+ years building backend services" and "Nice to have: Kubernetes" gets two items with those exact texts, kinds experience and skill, importance must and preferred; a model line that is not in the posting is dropped and counted in the report; two users scoring the same job later are judged against the same stored checklist; an age line produces the tag and no requirement.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/enrich/schema.test.ts (lenient parsing, cap), reconcile.test.ts (verbatim rule, ids, hash, replace-on-change, age tag on a cn fixture), agent.test.ts (the prompt asks for verbatim lines and excludes logistics), repository.test.ts.
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/enrich/schema.ts, agent.ts, reconcile.ts, repository.ts and their tests

[P1] Version bump, gradual re-enrichment and re-index (SM-6, SM-8; strategy 2.2 I7 (old rows keep serving until replaced))
CHANGE: server/src/features/jobs/enrich/schema.ts: ENRICH_VERSION 2 -> 3. Rows are re-enriched by the existing jobs-maintain step (features/jobs/ingest/maintain.ts selects "enrichVersion" < current) inside the existing daily enrichment budget (ENRICH_DAILY_JOBS), newest first; until a row is re-enriched it keeps its strings, has empty skillIds and no requirements, and every reader falls back (the estimate compares display strings, the scorer extracts requirements itself). Each finished enrichment already queues job.index (the hook of MKT-2H), so the search document and the vector pick up the canonical labels. Add to the enrichment log line the three counts canonical / unreviewed / dropped per job. Document in the handoff the expected number of model calls for the live index (one per live row) so the owner can raise or keep the daily budget; do not change the budget default.
ACCEPT: A row at version 2 is selected by maintenance and after one pass has skillIds, keywords with ids and, when the model ran, requirements; rows not yet re-enriched keep working on every surface; the job.index item is queued once per finished enrichment.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/enrich/service.test.ts (version check, already_enriched for version 3 rows, hook called), workers.test.ts.
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/enrich/schema.ts, service.ts and tests

[P2] Role candidates: add the nearest roles by title embedding when the title match is weak (SM-2 refinement; MATCH 4.5 point 3)
CHANGE: server/src/features/jobs/enrich/candidates.ts selectTaxonomyCandidates: when the deterministic title score is under 0.9 and the embeddings client is available, add up to 3 roles whose label vector is nearest to the title vector, inside the cap of 15, so the model always sees a plausible alternative. Role-label vectors (307 roles, labels in en and zh) are embedded once per worker process and model tag with purpose skill (no user data), kept in memory, and only inside the enrichment worker, never on a request path; when the client is unavailable the step is skipped silently. selectTaxonomyCandidates stays synchronous: the neighbours are computed in service.ts and passed in as extraIds.
ACCEPT: With a fake embeddings client the weak-title fixture gets three extra candidates and the exact-title fixture none; with the client unavailable the candidate list equals today's; the role vectors are requested once for many jobs.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/enrich/candidates.test.ts and service.test.ts with a fake client (call count, cap of 15, skip when unavailable).
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/enrich/candidates.ts, service.ts and tests

[P1] Enrichment says where its sponsorship reading comes from (JI-11, JI-7; strategy 1.5 "provider fields first"; ruling C18; the other half of MKT-3C's carry-through item)
CHANGE: MKT-3C (phase M3) added RAJob.sponsorshipSource (delivered by MKT-0) and lets a provider's flag fill RAJob.sponsorship only when the row has no posting quote. Complete the other side in server/src/features/jobs/enrich/reconcile.ts (the sponsorship block, lines 387-426 before this wave) and server/src/features/jobs/enrich/repository.ts (the select near line 80 and the update mapping near line 115): (a) when enrichment writes a sponsorship value together with a verified quote it also writes sponsorshipSource = 'posting_quote', replacing a stored 'provider:<id>' reading (the posting's own words win); (b) when enrichment finds no quote it leaves a stored 'provider:<id>' reading and its source untouched: it never clears a provider reading and never writes one; (c) when it removes a stored quote that no longer verifies (line 387) it sets sponsorship, sponsorshipEvidence and sponsorshipSource to null, except that a row whose stored source is 'provider:<id>' keeps sponsorship and its source and loses only the quote. No prompt change and no extra model call; the enrichment version bump of this bundle carries the change to live rows.
ACCEPT: A posting whose text says visa sponsorship is available ends with sponsorship 'offered', its quote and sponsorshipSource 'posting_quote', also when the row carried 'provider:activejobs_feed' before; a row with a provider reading and no sponsorship sentence in its text keeps both columns unchanged; a quote that fails verification is removed together with its source; a row enriched before this item (source null, quote present) is still read as quoted by every reader (MKT-3C and MKT-5C test sponsorshipEvidence as well as the source).
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/enrich/reconcile.test.ts (the three cases above and the unchanged no-signal case), server/src/features/jobs/enrich/repository.test.ts (the column is selected and written).
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/enrich/reconcile.ts, server/src/features/jobs/enrich/repository.ts, server/src/features/jobs/enrich/reconcile.test.ts, server/src/features/jobs/enrich/repository.test.ts
schema: RAJob.skillIds String[] with its GIN index and RAJob.requirements Json? (delivered by MKT-0)

bundles.title: Canonical skills in the estimate and a three-state keyword check; fit-card checklist UI; skills gate (SM-6 read path)
items:
[P0] The estimate compares canonical hard skills; the vocabulary is loaded before the first estimate (SM-6, SM-3; strategy 2.1 point 4 (hard canonical skills only); MATCH 4.4 point 3)
CHANGE: server/src/features/match/defaultService.ts: register the vocabulary loader once: registerMatchPreparer(() => skills.ready()) (the hook MKT-1F added in match/prepare.ts and MatchService.userContext awaits), so the synchronous estimate always reads a loaded vocabulary through skills.current(). server/src/features/match/context.ts toMatchJob: MatchJob gains skillIds (from the record; MKT-1F already selects the column) and each skillsDetail item its skillId. server/src/features/match/preScore.ts: new userSkillIdSet(user), memoised per MatchUser object, = userSkillIds(user.skills, user.resumeTextNorm) of server/src/features/skills (ids of listed skills plus reviewed skills whose alias appears as a whole word in the resume; an everyday-word alias counts only from the skill list). jobSkillList (lines 399-405) returns { skill, skillId, required, kind } de-duplicated by skillId when there is one, else by the existing termKey rule, labelled with the vocabulary's label for the request locale when reviewed, else displayTerm. skillsDimension: for an item with a reviewed id the state comes from evidenceFor(id, userSkillIdSet): shown counts its full weight, related counts half, not_shown nothing (weights as before: required 1, preferred 0.5); an item without a reviewed id is compared literally with the existing shownVia rule (so rows not yet re-enriched keep working) and an unreviewed or soft skill is never in numerator or denominator. splitSkills and overlapAndGap return canonical labels, so a card's top overlap and top gap use the usual spelling once. terms.ts stays the fallback for strings without ids; no table in it is removed.
ACCEPT: A job asking for "relational databases" (required) and a resume that lists PostgreSQL scores that item as related (half), not as missing and not as fully shown; a job that lists "Postgres" and "PostgreSQL" counts one skill; an unreviewed skill changes no score; for a job with empty skillIds the estimate equals what MKT-1F computed (same inputs, same number); the first estimate after a cold start sees the loaded vocabulary (the preparer was awaited).
TESTS: server/src/features/match/preScore.test.ts with a fixture vocabulary injected through the skills test seam: the three states and their weights, de-duplication by id, fallback for jobs without ids, soft and unreviewed excluded, labels per locale (zh-TW never a Simplified label); inputs.test.ts (toMatchJob carries ids).
FILES: server/src/features/match/preScore.ts, context.ts, defaultService.ts, testkit.ts, preScore.test.ts, inputs.test.ts

[P0] Keyword check with three states: Shown, Related, Not shown (SM-6 (Accepted when: "Not shown" precision >= 95%; no duplicate chips); strategy 2.3 step 5; MATCH 4.6)
CHANGE: server/src/features/match/keywordRows.ts buildKeywordRows (lines 47-123) and contract.ts KeywordRow: every item of the skills and keywords rows gains state: 'shown' | 'related' | 'not_shown', skillId, via (the more specific skill of the resume that counted, for related) and quote (for shown: the resume sentence that contains the term, at most 160 characters, verbatim; null when the term comes from the skill list only). found stays for older clients and is true for shown and related. Rules: shown = the canonical id is among the user's ids, or an alias of the skill appears as a whole word in the resume text (substring for CJK terms); related = evidenceFor says a more specific skill of the user shows this broader one (PostgreSQL for "relational databases"); not_shown = neither. Only hard skills and certifications with a reviewed id enter the two rows; a keyword without a reviewed id is not listed (it is neither claimed nor denied); items are de-duplicated by skillId across both rows and labelled with the canonical spelling. Row status (ratioStatus): shown counts 1, related 0.5. The existing literal path stays for skills of jobs that carry no ids yet. KeywordCheckResponse gains vocabularyAsOf (the snapshot time) so a support question can tell which vocabulary answered.
ACCEPT: Accepted when (SM-6): "Not shown" precision >= 95% on the labelled pairs of the next item; no duplicate chips. Added: the check never lists a skill the resume shows as not shown in the fixtures; "relational databases" with PostgreSQL on the resume reads related via PostgreSQL with no quote of its own; "Node.js", "node" and "NodeJS" produce one item; a shown item found in the text carries the sentence it was found in.
TESTS: server/src/features/match/keywordRows.test.ts (new): each state, quote extraction in English and Chinese, de-duplication across rows, items without reviewed ids omitted, legacy path for jobs without ids, row status arithmetic.
FILES: server/src/features/match/keywordRows.ts, contract.ts, keywordRows.test.ts

[P0] Skills gate: 100 labelled resume-job pairs, the harness suite, and invariant 7 enforced (SM-6; SM-1; strategy 2.6 skills gate; MATCH 6.2)
CHANGE: New server/src/features/match/eval/fixtures/skills/pairs.json: 100 synthetic resume-job pairs (at least 25 in Simplified Chinese, 10 in Traditional Chinese, 10 cross-language), each with the posting's skills and, per skill, the hand-assigned expected state shown | related | not_shown and a one-line reason; built on the personas and postings of MKT-1D where possible; "_synthetic": true; the vocabulary used is the committed seed plus a small fixture extension file in the same folder. New eval/suites/skills.suite.ts: runs buildKeywordRows on every pair and reports precision and recall per state; gate: precision of not_shown >= 0.95 (we must not tell people they lack what they have); it also reports duplicates (must be zero). server/src/features/match/eval/enforced.test.ts: raise the enforced phase to M4 so INV-7 (PostgreSQL is related evidence for "relational databases"; no skill listed twice) runs in npm test with the other nine.
ACCEPT: npm run eval:match prints the skills layer with precision of not_shown at or above 0.95 and zero duplicates; all ten invariants run in npm test and pass; npm run eval:match -- --enforce M4 exits 0 once the other M4 bundles are merged.
TESTS: The suite and enforced.test.ts are the tests; a shape test for pairs.json (100 pairs, language minimums, every expected state is one of the three).
FILES: server/src/features/match/eval/fixtures/skills/, server/src/features/match/eval/suites/skills.suite.ts, server/src/features/match/eval/enforced.test.ts

[P1] Fit card UI: three-state keyword rows and the requirement checklist (SM-6, SM-8; MATCH 4.6 table "Shown as", 4.8)
CHANGE: components/features/match/KeywordCheck.tsx: render each item by state: shown -> "Your resume shows it" with the quote when there is one; related -> "Related: your resume shows {term}" (the person decides whether to add the exact term; offer the existing "add to resume" path, never an automatic edit); not_shown -> "Not in your resume". Counts read "{shown} shown, {related} related, of {total}". components/features/match/FitAnalysisCard.tsx and WhyYouFit.tsx: when the fit carries requirements (MatchFitView.requirements, filled by scorer v4; empty before), list them grouped must then preferred, each with its status (Met, Partly, Not shown; not_applicable items are not listed), the posting line verbatim and the resume quote verbatim when there is one; on GoApply the AI-written parts keep their AI label (AiGeneratedBadge) and no line uses visa wording. With no requirements the card renders as today. hooks/match/useKeywordCheck.ts: types only. New English strings under fit.keywordCheck.* and fit.requirements.* in i18n/staging/fit.en.json, second person, no brand literal; a status is never worded as a verdict on the person ("Not shown in your resume", never "You lack").
ACCEPT: A keyword row shows the three states with their own wording and the quote; a fit with a checklist shows must-haves first with posting line and resume quote; an estimate (no checklist) renders unchanged; GoApply shows the AI label on model-written text; npm run check passes (design and copy gates).
TESTS: components/features/match/match.test.tsx: the three states, counts, checklist grouping and quotes, empty checklist, GoApply label; hooks/match tests compile.
FILES: components/features/match/KeywordCheck.tsx, FitAnalysisCard.tsx, WhyYouFit.tsx, DimensionList.tsx, labels.ts, match.module.css, match.test.tsx, hooks/match/useKeywordCheck.ts, i18n/staging/fit.en.json
schema: reads RAJob.skillIds and the skillId inside RAJob.skillsDetail items (columns delivered by MKT-0, values written by MKT-4D in the same phase; every reader here falls back to display strings while they are empty)

bundles.title: Feed: hybrid retrieval by reciprocal rank, the residual text as a ranking query, then the ranking refinements (SM-7, SM-9 feed part, SM-12)
items:
[P0] Three retrieval legs as SQL builders under the same scope and filter predicates (SM-7; strategy 2.1 point 3; MATCH 4.9 retrieval table)
CHANGE: New server/src/features/feed/hybridSql.ts (the leg builders live in their own file and import scopePredicates, filterPredicates, FEED_COLUMNS, retrievalSql, qPredicateSql and wideQPredicateSql from feed/sql.ts; the one edit to sql.ts is the widened typed-query predicate described below). Keep retrievalSql (sql.ts line 420) as leg A (recency). Add: lexicalLegSql(input, tsQuery): the same scopePredicates and filterPredicates, plus j."searchTsv" @@ to_tsquery('simple', $q), ORDER BY ts_rank_cd(j."searchTsv", to_tsquery('simple', $q)) DESC, j."postedAt" DESC NULLS LAST, j."id" DESC, LIMIT n; $q is built by toTsQuery of server/src/features/retrieval/segment.ts (the OR of the segmented tokens; the same function that segmented the document). denseLegSql(input, vectorLiteral, modelTag): the same predicates, JOIN "RAJobEmbedding" e ON e."jobId" = j."id" AND e."model" = $tag AND e."market" = $market, ORDER BY e."embedding" <=> $v::halfvec(1024), LIMIT n: an exact distance over the rows the filters leave, no approximate index. Both take from = the feed's age floor (floorOf: postedWithinDays or FEED_LIMITS.maxAgeDays 120), not the 14-day first window, so the best match that is not among the newest 400 can be found. The typed q: the q predicate of sql.ts (qPredicateSql, exported by MKT-2H) requires searchText ILIKE or a trigram match on the thin searchText (title + company + 10 skills). For the feed list build every leg with the filter fields minus q (the fields argument of retrievalSql and filterPredicates) and add wideQPredicateSql(q), defined in feed/sql.ts next to qPredicateSql (so sql.ts never imports hybridSql.ts), through the existing extra argument: (j."searchTsv" @@ to_tsquery('simple', $q) OR qPredicateSql(q)), so a term that appears only in the description is findable while rows not indexed yet (searchTsv null) still match through searchText; for input shorter than 3 Latin characters use qPredicateSql alone. The dense leg does not apply the q predicate (it is the leg that finds synonyms, adjacent titles and other languages); every other predicate applies to all legs. This bundle owns feed/sql.ts in M4 (the Taiwan filter bundle MKT-5F edits it one phase later, on top of this change): case 'q' of predicateFor returns wideQPredicateSql(q) too (same short-input rule), so the count, sample and alert statements find a term that appears only in the description exactly as the list does; nothing else in sql.ts changes. Limits come from FEED_LIMITS.legLimit 200 and rrfK 60 (added by MKT-2H); retrievalLimit stays 400 as the cap of the union.

New retrieveHybrid(ctx, filters, sort, state) used by firstWindow (lines 322-332) for the sorts recommended and best_fit, and for newest only when a query text is present; the deadline and highest_pay sorts and browse lists keep today's single statement. Legs run in parallel (Promise.all over repo.queryRows), 200 rows each: A = today's window (14 days, widened to 45 under 60 rows); B = lexical; C = dense. Query text for B and C: the typed q when present; else the relevance text (the residual of a natural-language search, next item); else, for a personalised user only, B uses the titles of the user's recent roles and their top skills (at most 24 tokens) and C uses the user vector (userVector of server/src/features/retrieval: resume, else intent). bundles.title: Scorer v4: requirement checklist with anchored statuses, server-computed numbers, resume-first prompt, pinned version per market (SM-8)
items:
[P0] Scorer v4 agent: the model fills a checklist, never a number; resume first for prompt caching (SM-8; strategy 2.1 point 5, 2.3 step 7; MATCH 2.4, 4.8)
CHANGE: server/src/roboapply/v2/agents/RAJobMatchScorerAgent.ts: add RAJobMatchScorerV4Agent beside the v3 class (v3 stays for the rollback switch and its tests). Output schema (strict JSON, parsed with the same defensive parser style as the v3 parseOutput, lines 527-570): { requirements: [{ id, kind: skill | experience | education | domain | scope, text, importance: must | preferred, status: met | partly | not_shown | not_applicable, evidence }], level: { post, resume, direction: match | post_higher | post_lower }, domain: { status: direct | adjacent | unrelated | not_stated, evidence }, trajectory: { status: toward | neutral | away | no_history, evidence }, strengths[<=5], gaps[<=5], summary }. No score, total or percentage anywhere in the output; a summary that states a number is dropped (SUMMARY_NUMBER, line 387). Prompt: keep the persona line, the second-person rule and hard rules 3-5 and 7 of the v3 prompt (never invent, never judge school tier, age, gender, nationality, ethnicity, family, photo, 籍贯 or 政治面貌; gaps are observations about the resume); replace the "score each 0-100" section with the checklist instructions and the anchors: met = the resume shows it plainly, with a verbatim resume quote as evidence; partly = related or shorter experience, with a quote; not_shown = no evidence in the resume (evidence empty); not_applicable = the line is not a requirement of the candidate (for example a benefits line). When the input carries the posting's stored requirement list, the model must return exactly those ids and texts and only fill status and evidence; when it carries none, the model extracts at most 12 requirement lines verbatim from the posting first. level uses the six level names of SENIORITY_LEVELS for post and resume. Input order for provider prompt caching (the v3 formatInput, lines 495-525, puts the job first and the resume last): system rubric, then "## Candidate profile" and "## Candidate resume" (identical across the up to 25 jobs precomputed for one user), then the job post and the logistics facts last. Temperature 0 (getTemperature), max tokens 2,400. Export SCORER_V4_PROMPT_VERSION = 'scorer_v4' and the input and output types.
ACCEPT: A valid model answer parses into the typed checklist; an answer with a numeric score field is accepted only after the field is ignored and never used; an answer missing level or with an unknown status throws (the caller falls back to the estimate and stores nothing); the formatted input starts with the resume block for two different jobs of one user byte-identically up to the job section.
TESTS: server/src/roboapply/v2/agents/RAJobMatchScorerAgent.test.ts: parser cases (valid, unknown enum, missing parts, stray number, evidence caps), the prompt contains the anchors and none of "score each", the resume-first prefix equality, the stored-requirements mode keeps ids. The model is never called in tests.
FILES: server/src/roboapply/v2/agents/RAJobMatchScorerAgent.ts, RAJobMatchScorerAgent.test.ts

[P0] The server computes every component from the checklist; evidence is verified; the checklist is stored once per posting (SM-8 (server-computed numbers); strategy 2.1 point 5; MATCH 4.8 anchors)
CHANGE: New server/src/features/match/scorerV4.ts (pure): componentsFromChecklist(out, { weights, logistics, sources }) -> MatchDimension[] and RequirementCheck[]. Verification first: a requirement text must be a verbatim substring of the posting text the model saw (normalizeForGuard of match/evidence.ts), else the item is dropped; a status met or partly whose evidence is not a verbatim substring of the PII-stripped resume the model saw is downgraded to not_shown with empty evidence (never tell someone they have what the text does not show; never keep an unverifiable claim). Numbers: points met 1, partly 0.5, not_shown 0, not_applicable excluded; weight must 1, preferred 0.5. skills component = 100 x sum(points x weight) / sum(weight) over items of kind skill and experience (not stated when there is none). title_level = level direction: same level 100, one level apart 60, two levels 25, more 0 (distance between level.post and level.resume on the six-level scale), halved when an education item of importance must is not_shown and, on GoApply, when a stated 届别 excludes the user (the same eligibility rule the estimate applies). industry = domain: direct 100, adjacent 60, unrelated 20, not_stated -> not stated. career_path = trajectory: toward 100, neutral 60, away 25, no_history -> not stated. logistics = the deterministic logisticsDimension as today (never judged by the model). The total stays combineDimensions over the stated components (the stored AI total keeps today's arithmetic; the estimate is brought to this scale by the calibration of MKT-1F). MatchService.scoreJob (model-call section, lines 522-629): when the pinned rubric is fit_v4 call the v4 agent with the stored RAJob.requirements items (MatchJobRecord.requirements, carried since MKT-1F) or none; when the job had none and the verified checklist has at least one item, write it to the job through a new MatchRepo.saveJobRequirements(jobId, { v: 1, contentHash, model, extractedAt, items }) guarded so the first writer wins (UPDATE … WHERE "requirements" IS NULL); save the score row with dimensions, explanation { strengths, gaps, rationale, requirements: RequirementCheck[], level, domain, trajectory, estimateAtScore, responseLanguage }, promptVersion scorer_v4, rubricVersion fit_v4, jobContentHash. fit.ts and aiView return requirements on MatchFitView (the field exists since MKT-1F). The locale rewrite path (lines 554-568) rewrites strengths, gaps and summary only: statuses are enums, so the number is language-independent and "rewrite in my language" never changes it.
ACCEPT: For a recorded model answer: the skills component equals the hand-computed weighted share; a met with an invented quote becomes not_shown and lowers the component; a requirement line that is not in the posting disappears; two users scored on the same job read the same stored checklist ids; the stored row carries rubric fit_v4; a locale rewrite changes prose only; nothing the model returns can set a component or the total directly.
TESTS: server/src/features/match/scorerV4.test.ts (each anchor, weights, verification, eligibility halving, not-stated cases, totals by hand), MatchService.test.ts (v4 path with a fake agent: stored-requirements mode, first-writer rule, row fields, rewrite path, fallback to the estimate on a parser error), fit.test.ts (requirements on the view).

CHANGE: server/src/features/match/config.ts currentScorerPin(brand) (added by MKT-1F): rubric from MATCH_SCORER_RUBRIC through brandEnv (default fit_v4; fit_v3 is the rollback), prompt scorer_v4 or scorer_v3 accordingly, model = the resolved scorer model of the brand (LLM_MATCHING_MODEL, GoApply CN_LLM_MATCHING_MODEL when set, else the shared one: server/src/features/match/scorerRoute.ts keeps deciding whether the route is allowed). One version at a time per market: rows of another model, prompt or rubric keep serving with stale true (rule of MKT-1F) and are replaced by the precompute cron within the existing budgets (25 a day per user, the brand budget), newest feed candidates first; there is no bulk invalidation. Borderline rule in MatchService: when a new v4 total lands within 3 points of a tier edge (45, 65, 80 or the configured MATCH_TIERS), the stored tier is the tier on the same side of that edge as the v2 estimate computed for the same inputs (estimateAtScore); no second model call; the score itself is stored as computed. server/src/features/match/cron.ts: the precompute pick order becomes the order of the feed list it reads (the fused, ranked order of the candidate ids) instead of re-sorting by the estimate (the pre.sort call in queueForUser), and a candidate is skipped only when it has a row matching the current pin and job hash. workers.ts: the job.score payload carries nothing new; the handler passes the pin through.
ACCEPT: With MATCH_SCORER_RUBRIC unset new scores are fit_v4 on both brands; setting it to fit_v3 writes v3 rows again without a deploy; after a model change a user's existing fits stay visible and are re-scored gradually; a v4 total of 66 with an estimate of 58 is stored with tier possible and a total of 69 with tier good; the cron queues candidates in feed order and never more than the per-user and brand budgets.
TESTS: server/src/features/match/MatchService.test.ts (borderline cases at each edge, both sides), cron.test.ts (pick order, pin freshness, budgets unchanged), config tests for the pin and the brand fallback, scorerV3.test.ts kept green behind the rollback switch.
FILES: server/src/features/match/config.ts, MatchService.ts, cron.ts, workers.ts, scorerRoute.ts and the tests named above

[P1] Scorer stability and validity suite for the harness (SM-8 (Accepted when: ICC >= 0.85; tier flips under 5%); SM-1; strategy 2.6 scorer gate)
CHANGE: New server/src/features/match/eval/suites/scorer.suite.ts and eval/fixtures/scorer/. Offline part (CI): replays recorded model answers from fixtures/scorer/recorded.<market>.json (written by the live mode: three runs on 100 persona-posting pairs with the pinned model, checked in after the owner reviews them; they are answers about synthetic personas and postings) through componentsFromChecklist and reports the intraclass correlation over the three runs, the share of pairs whose tier differs between runs, and, when an audit file with human grades exists, the Spearman correlation of score against grade; gates: ICC >= 0.85, tier flips under 5%, Spearman >= 0.6 and not below the v3 value recorded the same way. Until recordings exist the suite prints no_fixture (it does not fail CI, and no number is invented). It always runs a deterministic self-check with three hand-written answers per pair for 10 pairs to prove the pipeline (parser, verification, arithmetic, borderline rule) is stable for identical input. Live part: the runner of MKT-1D calls the real scorer three times per pair and writes the recording.
ACCEPT: Offline with the hand-written set: ICC 1 and zero flips; with a recording the three metrics are printed against their gates; without one the row reads no_fixture; the live run is the owner's step and its report states model id, date and sample size.
TESTS: The suite is the test; a unit test of the replay loader (shape, three runs per pair, market tags).
FILES: server/src/features/match/eval/suites/scorer.suite.ts, server/src/features/match/eval/fixtures/scorer/

bundles.title: Search surfaces outside the feed: planner relevance terms and the job-search API on both brands, Assistant job tools with cited ids (SM-9)
items:
[P0] The planner returns relevance terms; unsupported constraints stay visible as unchecked (SM-9; strategy 2.3 step 8; MATCH 4.10 points 1-2)
CHANGE: server/src/job-search/agent.ts PLANNER_PROMPT (lines 21-27): add to the schema "relevanceTerms": up to 5 short topical phrases taken from the request (an industry, a product area, a technology, a mission: "climate startups", "Rust", "developer tools") that are neither enforced by the schema nor conditions on pay, visa, benefits, hours, time zone, commute or company size; those conditions stay in unverifiedPreferences as today and are never placed in relevanceTerms. The rule "never claim these facts were checked" stays. server/src/job-search/agent-validation.ts parseAgentPlan (line 49): add relevanceTerms to the allowed set (line 53) and validate it: optional array, at most 5 items, each a string of 2 to 60 characters with no control characters and no URL, de-duplicated case-insensitively; an invalid value is dropped, not fatal (the plan stays usable). types.ts AgentPlan and the agent result: agent.rankedBy = the terms. resolvePlan (line 82) passes them through. The feed reads them through its existing planner dependency (PlannerPlan.relevanceTerms is already accepted by planToFilters since MKT-2H). Both brands use the same planner; on GoApply the aiAllowed check added by PAR-8 stays in front of the model call.
ACCEPT: For "remote backend roles at climate startups, ideally using Rust, paying over 150k" the plan holds queries ["backend engineer"] (or the planner's wording), remote true, relevanceTerms ["climate startups", "Rust"] and the pay phrase in unverifiedPreferences; a plan with 9 relevance terms or a URL in one is still accepted with the bad values dropped; the /feed/nl-query response then carries those terms in rankedBy.
TESTS: server/src/job-search/agent.test.ts and a new agent-validation test file: allowed field, caps, dropped values, pass-through into the result; the planner model is a fake.
FILES: server/src/job-search/agent.ts, agent-validation.ts, types.ts, agent.test.ts, server/src/job-search/agent-validation.test.ts

[P0] The job-search API reads our index through the same retrieval pipeline (SM-9; D5 (natural-language job search works on both brands); MATCH 4.10 points 3-4; parity plan 3.10)
CHANGE: server/src/job-search/service.ts: the GoApply provider index (added by PAR-8: public market cn rows read through the feed's exported read function) passes the request's query as q and the plan's relevance terms as relevance (the parameter that function accepts since MKT-2H), so an API search and an in-app search of the same words go through the same legs and the same fusion; no second ranking code exists in job-search. The response of the planned search (server/src/job-search/agent.ts) gains agent.rankedBy and keeps agent.unverifiedPreferences; openapi.ts documents both with the sentence that ranking terms are not verified facts about a job. RoboApply: the live provider fan-out stays as the public API product (its results are provider results in provider order and carry no fit); nothing in the app ranks them by a separate path. A result with no usable apply link is still dropped on both brands (normalization.ts unchanged).
ACCEPT: On a GoApply host a planned search with relevance terms returns index rows in the fused order (a fixture row that mentions the terms precedes an equally recent one that does not) and makes no outbound provider call; the RoboApply API response is unchanged except for the added rankedBy field; the OpenAPI document validates.
TESTS: server/src/job-search/service.test.ts (index provider passes q and relevance to a fake read function; no provider fetch on GoApply), agent.test.ts (rankedBy in the response), routes.test.ts (shape unchanged for existing clients).
FILES: server/src/job-search/service.ts, agent.ts, openapi.ts, types.ts and the tests named above

[P0] Assistant job tools: the user's imports are included, fits come from getFits, and the card shows exactly the jobs the model cites (SM-9 (Accepted when: the card shows exactly the cited jobs); strategy 2.3 step 8; MATCH 3.5 (two findings), 4.10 point 3)
CHANGE: server/src/features/copilot/tools/jobs.ts. (1) Lists pass through the feed seam, so search_jobs with keywords now uses hybrid retrieval with no change here; keep q as the typed query. (2) Imports: addedRows (lines 69-95) reads the stored fit of each added job one after another; replace the loop with one getFits call for all ids (one batch read, never a model call). top_fit_jobs (lines 232-246) lists only what the feed preview returns, which leaves out imports whose posting has no date: merge the user's added jobs (ctx.areas.addedJobs) with the preview rows, order all by the same Fit (score, then kind ai first), and return at most the limit. search_jobs without keywords stays the saved search; with keywords it already looks through imports. (3) Cited ids. Today every search tool emits a job_list card with all rows it returned and the prompt tells the model to describe the whole list (copilot/prompt.ts line 35). New tool show_jobs({ jobIds: 1..8 ids, note? }) in tools/jobs.ts and tools/registry.ts: it accepts only ids returned by a tool earlier in this turn or shown in the recent cards (the allowedJobIds set CopilotService already keeps, lines 490 and 607), loads the rows from the turn's tool results (kept in the tool context, no new query) and emits the job_list card with exactly those jobs in the given order. search_jobs, top_fit_jobs and added_jobs stop emitting the card themselves and return their rows and ids as data. Prompt (prompt.ts): replace line 35 with: "After a search, call show_jobs with the ids of the jobs you are going to talk about, in the order you mention them. The card shows exactly those jobs. Never name a job you did not pass to show_jobs. To narrow a list by a rule (only remote, only posts that list pay), call the search tool again with arguments." CopilotService.ts (tool loop, lines 601-622): if the turn ends and a search tool returned rows but show_jobs was never called, emit the card with all returned rows (today's behaviour, so nothing is lost) and log copilot_guard_hit kind jobs_not_cited. Quick action similar_jobs (prompt.ts line 61) calls a new tool similar_jobs({ jobId }) that reads the Similar jobs list of the job-detail service (jobDetailService.similar, by job vector since MKT-2F and MKT-2H) instead of a title search; the job-detail area itself is not edited. The visitor variant (publicSearchJobs) keeps its card: visitors have no cited-id step.
ACCEPT: A model that searches (5 rows) and cites 2 ids gets a card with exactly those 2 jobs in that order; citing an id no tool returned is refused and logged; a turn without show_jobs still shows the full list and logs jobs_not_cited; "the job I added at Acme" is found and "my best fits" includes an added job with a strong fit; an added job's fit on the card equals the job page's; no tool calls the scorer except analyze_fit.
TESTS: server/src/features/copilot/__tests__/tools.test.ts (show_jobs acceptance and refusal, order, imports in top_fit_jobs, one getFits call), service.test.ts (card held back until cited, fallback and log, similar_jobs quick action), guard.test.ts unchanged and green.
FILES: server/src/features/copilot/tools/jobs.ts, tools/registry.ts, prompt.ts, CopilotService.ts, areas.ts, types.ts, __tests__/tools.test.ts, __tests__/service.test.ts, __tests__/areaFakes.ts

[P1] Assistant job-list card on the web renders the cited list (SM-9; MATCH 3.5)
CHANGE: components/features/copilot/cards/JobListCard.tsx and model.ts: the card renders the items of the show_jobs card in the order given, with the optional note line, the fit chip (kind and confidence from the same Fit fields the feed card uses) and "added by you" for imports; it no longer assumes the list is a complete search result (remove any "N results" wording that implies completeness; show "Jobs mentioned in this answer" from assistant.jobList.title). When a card arrives through the fallback path (the model cited nothing) the title is the existing search title. Strings in i18n/staging/assistant.en.json.
ACCEPT: The card shows exactly the jobs of the card payload, in order, with no count that implies a full result set; an import shows its label; npm run check passes.
TESTS: components/features/copilot/cards tests (order, labels, fallback title).
FILES: components/features/copilot/cards/JobListCard.tsx, components/features/copilot/cards/model.ts, i18n/staging/assistant.en.json and the card tests

bundles.title: Licensed feed (Active Jobs DB): hourly window sync with the expired feed behind the quota gate; Active Jobs DB for the mainland
items:
[P0] Quota gate and transports for the licensed feed (JI-7; strategy M-2, 1.2 tier 1, 7 item 1)
CHANGE: The feed must run by itself the day a paid plan exists and must not run on the free BASIC plan (25 requests, 250 jobs a month). server/src/features/jobs/ingest/quota.ts: feedGate(env, now) -> { open: boolean, reason: 'plan_too_small' | 'no_key' | 'disabled' | 'exhausted' | 'ok', monthlyJobs: number | null }. monthlyJobs = the larger of the stored snapshot's jobsLimit for provider 'activejobs' (MKT-3A reads x-ratelimit-jobs-limit from every response) and env FANTASTIC_MONTHLY_JOBS (the plan size the owner bought, for a transport whose responses do not state it). The gate is open only when monthlyJobs >= 20,000 (constant FEED_MIN_MONTHLY_JOBS), a key for the chosen transport exists, FANTASTIC_FEED_DISABLED is not true and the snapshot is not exhausted. Daily job budget: INGEST_FEED_DAILY_JOBS, default floor(monthlyJobs / 31); jobs returned are counted in RAProviderUsage.jobsReturned under 'activejobs' (and 'activejobs:cn' for the mainland sync) and a fetch is refused once the day's jobs reach the budget. Transport in server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raFantasticJobs.ts: add feedRequest(path, params, opts) next to the search call, sharing the breaker, timeout (25 s) and quota listener: 'rapidapi' (default; host active-jobs-db.p.rapidapi.com with RAPID_API_KEY, as today) or 'direct' when FANTASTIC_TRANSPORT=direct (host data.fantastic.jobs with FANTASTIC_API_KEY). The direct API's authentication header and exact paths are taken from the vendor's documentation (https://developer.fantastic.jobs/documentation/endpoints/new-jobs and /expired-jobs), read in the session and cited with the date in the file header; if they cannot be confirmed, the header name is read from FANTASTIC_API_KEY_HEADER with no default and the direct transport reports 'no_key' until it is set (never a guessed header). Paths default to '/active-ats' and '/expired-ats' (INTL note 6.2) and can be overridden with FANTASTIC_FEED_PATH / FANTASTIC_EXPIRED_PATH because the RapidAPI listing has renamed routes before (file header, lines 24-25 and 552-554). Keys are read per call and never logged. The admin System panel already shows state 'gated' for a plan under 20,000 (MKT-3F).
ACCEPT: The first 'Accepted when' clause of JI-7: with the snapshot of today's plan (jobsLimit 250) feedGate is closed with reason plan_too_small and no feed request is ever built; with jobsLimit 100,000 (or FANTASTIC_MONTHLY_JOBS=100000 and a key) it is open and the daily job budget is 3,225; FANTASTIC_FEED_DISABLED=true closes it; with FANTASTIC_TRANSPORT=direct and no header name configured the gate reports no_key; no key value appears in a log or error string.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/quota.test.ts (gate table, budget arithmetic), server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raFantasticJobs.test.ts with a mocked fetch (both transports build the documented URL and headers; listener called; 429 opens the breaker).
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/quota.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/quota.test.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/config.ts, server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raFantasticJobs.ts, server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raFantasticJobs.test.ts

[P0] Window-sync adapter: one backfill, then hourly windows paged by offset and resumed across cron runs (JI-7; strategy 1.2 tier 1; INTL note 6.2, 8.1 M5)
CHANGE: New server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/fantasticFeed.ts: JobSourceAdapter with provider 'activejobs_feed' (declared in MKT-1C; it writes sourceBoard 'activejobs' and externalId 'activejobs:<id>', the same rows the search adapter addresses), kind 'cursor', markets ['intl','cn'], costModel 'per_job', isEnabledFor(market) = feedGate open (and, for cn, the mainland switch of item 6), isEnabled = the gate, dailyCallLimit null (it is metered in jobs by item 1, not in calls). The standing query's params.cursor is JSON { v: 1, phase: 'backfill' | 'hourly', window: '7d' | '1h', offset, highWater: ISO | null, lastHourlyAt, lastExpiredHourlyAt, lastExpiredDailyAt, lastExpiredMonthlyAt }. One fetch = one request: phase backfill -> time_frame=7d, limit=1000, offset; a full page (1,000 rows) answers exhausted false with offset + 1000 (so paging resumes on the next lease or the next cron run, under MKT-3A's per-tick share); a short page ends the backfill and switches to hourly. Phase hourly: when at least 60 minutes have passed since lastHourlyAt, request time_frame=1h&limit=1000 and page by offset the same way; highWater = the newest date_created seen; after an outage longer than the window (lastHourlyAt more than 2 h ago) send date_created_gte=highWater instead of relying on the 1 h window. Every request carries description_format=text and include_basic_organization_details=true and the location filter of item 4. Rows are mapped with inputFromFantasticJob (server/src/features/jobs/normalize/adapters.ts 39-95, extended in item 5) and returned as jobs; the pipeline upserts and dedupes them (K2 collapses a feed row onto a board row for the same posting). Register the adapter in server/src/features/jobs/ingest/providers.ts ensureBuiltinAdapters (19-31) and let adaptersForBrand include it for RoboApply after 'activejobs' (the on-demand search adapter stays for interactive use). server/src/features/jobs/ingest/planner.ts: while the feed gate is open, the activejobs SEARCH adapter plans no seo_seed tuples (the feed covers the breadth; a seed search would pay per job for rows the feed already returns).
ACCEPT: The second 'Accepted when' clause of JI-7: on a plan with at least 20,000 jobs a month an hourly window pages by offset (two fixture pages of 1,000 and 240 rows produce two requests with offset 0 and 1000, the first answering exhausted false); a run interrupted between the pages resumes at offset 1000 from the stored cursor; a second fetch within the hour makes no request; the backfill runs once and never again after the phase switched; with the gate closed the adapter is disabled, the planner plans nothing for it and runJobsIngest makes no feed call.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/fantasticFeed.test.ts with an injected transport and fake clock: phases, paging, resume from a serialised cursor, the hourly cadence, the outage high-water path, budget refusal; server/src/features/jobs/ingest/planner.test.ts: no seeds on the search adapter while the gate is open.
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/fantasticFeed.ts (new), server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/fantasticFeed.test.ts (new), server/src/features/jobs/ingest/providers.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/planner.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/planner.test.ts

[P0] The vendor's expired feed closes our rows by id (JI-7; strategy 1.5 closure; INTL note 6.2, 7.2)
CHANGE: Today a feed row lives until posted + 45 days although the vendor rechecks every job daily. In server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/fantasticFeed.ts, after the hourly new-jobs window is drained, the same fetch cycle runs the expired feed by its own clocks in the cursor: every hour expired?time_frame=1h; once a day after 01:00 UTC time_frame=1d (catches what an hourly run missed); once a month time_frame=1m (reconciliation). The endpoint returns vendor ids only: map each to externalId 'activejobs:<id>' and return them as closedExternalIds with closeReason 'source_removed' (the pipeline archives matching open rows of sourceBoard 'activejobs' and the upsert revives a row the vendor lists again). An expired id we never stored is ignored. Expired calls cost requests, not jobs: count them as calls. Rows of this provider keep the 45-day default expiry as a backstop (MKT-3C's rule for aggregators) and take the vendor's date_validthrough when it is stated.
ACCEPT: The third 'Accepted when' clause of JI-7: an expired-feed fixture containing the id of a stored open row archives that row with closeReason 'source_removed' and leaves other rows alone; the hourly, daily (only after 01:00 UTC) and monthly expired calls each run at most once per period according to the cursor; a transport error on the expired call does not lose the new-jobs rows of the same fetch and is retried on the next cycle.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/fantasticFeed.test.ts: the three clocks with a fake clock, id mapping, error isolation; fixture server/src/features/jobs/normalize/__fixtures__/fantastic-expired.json (ids only).
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/fantasticFeed.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/fantasticFeed.test.ts, server/src/features/jobs/normalize/__fixtures__/fantastic-expired.json (new)

[P1] Filters that keep the bill down: countries, and exclude_source only for an ATS we already cover with at least 200 enabled boards (JI-7; strategy 1.2 tier 1; critic C14; INTL note 6.2)
CHANGE: In the feed adapter's request builder: (1) location = an OR of full country names (the API wants names, not codes; use fantasticCountryName from server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raFantasticJobs.ts, line 158, and the OR syntax the vendor's endpoint documentation gives) for the ISO codes in INGEST_FEED_COUNTRIES, default 'US,CA,GB,IE,DE,FR,NL,ES,IT,SE,AU,SG,TW' (the brand's markets per strategy 1.2 and 1.3; a tunable default: the owner trims it after measuring volume with the vendor's count endpoint). The mainland standing query (market cn) sends location = 'China' only. (2) exclude_source: an ATS is excluded only once our own seed for it holds at least 200 enabled boards (constant FEED_EXCLUDE_MIN_BOARDS = 200): count RACareerSiteSource rows with enabled true grouped by ats (one cheap query per fetch cycle, cached for 10 minutes) and map our ats ids to the vendor's source names ('greenhouse', 'lever.co', 'ashby', 'smartrecruiters', 'workable', 'recruitee', 'personio', as listed in INTL note 6.2; confirm each name against the vendor's documentation and keep the map in one table with the doc date). Below 200 the ATS is NOT excluded: its jobs on boards we have not discovered would otherwise come from neither side; K2 dedupe keeps the board row canonical for the ones we do read. (3) Agencies are not excluded (the product keeps them and labels them); organization_agency is not sent. (4) No title or taxonomy filter by default; INGEST_FEED_TAXONOMIES (comma list, vendor taxonomy names) is passed as the vendor's taxonomy filter when set, for a plan that needs a cap.
ACCEPT: The last 'Accepted when' clause of JI-7: with 180 enabled Greenhouse boards and 210 enabled Lever boards the request excludes lever.co and not greenhouse; with no enabled boards nothing is excluded; the intl request names the configured countries by full name and the cn request names China only; an unknown ISO code in INGEST_FEED_COUNTRIES is skipped and logged once, never sent as a code.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/fantasticFeed.test.ts with a fake db for the board counts: threshold at 199 / 200, the name map, country names, the cn query.
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/fantasticFeed.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/fantasticFeed.test.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/config.ts

[P1] The feed's own fields are mapped first: level, work arrangement, employment type, skills, taxonomy, employer domain, pay, and the sponsorship flag as the provider's reading (JI-7; strategy 1.5 "provider fields first"; INTL note 8.2 S3)
CHANGE: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/adapters.ts inputFromFantasticJob (39-95) already maps experience level, key skills, work arrangement, employment type, salary and the organisation website. Complete it for the feed payload (record a fixture from the vendor's documented sample, or from one real response once a plan exists; until then build server/src/features/jobs/normalize/__fixtures__/fantastic-feed.json from the documented field list and mark it SYNTHETIC in the fixtures README): (1) companyFacts.domain = domain_derived when present (it feeds the employer-domain dedupe key of MKT-3C) and industries / size / headcount when include_basic_organization_details returns them, each with source 'provider:activejobs'; (2) sponsorshipProvider from the vendor's visa-sponsorship flag (ai_visa_sponsorship: true -> 'offered', false -> 'not_offered', absent -> null): MKT-3C stores it as sponsorship with sponsorshipSource 'provider:activejobs_feed' only when no posting quote exists, so it is always shown as the provider's reading and never as a fact; (3) taxonomyId: map the vendor's taxonomy labels (ai_taxonomies_a) to our tree through a small table in this file that contains ONLY labels seen in the fixture or the vendor's documentation, each mapped to an L1 / L3 id or to null; an unmapped label falls back to the title dictionary (never guess a mapping); (4) expiresAt from date_validthrough; postedAt from date_posted, else date_created with postedAtEstimated true; (5) applyIsDirect = source_type 'ats' (unchanged). Never mapped (H9, D3): LinkedIn organisation fields, recruiter or hiring-manager names, applicant or view counts. With these fields present the normalizer's coverage.complete lets enrichment skip the model call for the row (existing rule, not changed here).
ACCEPT: A feed fixture row yields seniority from the provider's level, a provider work model, skills, a companyFacts.domain, sponsorshipProvider 'offered' and an expiry from date_validthrough; a row without the flag yields sponsorshipProvider null; an unmapped taxonomy label leaves taxonomyId unset; no LinkedIn or recruiter field is present on the input (asserted by key list); the existing fantastic.json fixture tests still pass.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/adapters.fantastic.test.ts (new) over the two fixtures: every mapped field, the never-mapped list, fallbacks.
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/adapters.ts, server/src/features/jobs/normalize/adapters.fantastic.test.ts (new), server/src/features/jobs/normalize/__fixtures__/fantastic-feed.json (new), server/src/features/jobs/normalize/__fixtures__/fantastic.json, server/src/features/jobs/normalize/__fixtures__/README.md

[P1] Active Jobs DB serves GoApply behind the same quota gate; usage is counted under activejobs:cn and no user data is sent (JC-6; strategy 1.4 tier 1, M-6; CN note 4.3, 6 tier 1 item 5)
CHANGE: Mainland roles of multinationals (Workday, SuccessFactors and other ATSs with no public API) are reachable only through this feed. (1) Feed: the activejobs_feed adapter creates its standing query for market cn (ensureBankSyncQueries does this for a cursor adapter whose markets include cn) and isEnabledFor('cn') is true only when the feed gate is open AND CN_ACTIVEJOBS_ENABLED is not false (default on once the gate is open: D5, a paid plan is the only gate). The cn sync sends location=China, the same window paging and expired handling, and counts jobs and calls under usageKey('activejobs','cn') = 'activejobs:cn' with its own daily job budget INGEST_FEED_CN_DAILY_JOBS (default 20% of the daily feed budget). Rows are written in market cn only when their resolved location is in mainland China (a row the vendor returns for 'China' that resolves to Hong Kong, Macau or Taiwan is dropped for cn and counted wrong_market; it reaches RoboApply through the intl sync). Every cn row keeps its employer apply URL and shows 来源 with the original publisher (the parity wave's source line); the mainland fraud rules and text scrubbing run through the existing cn hooks. (2) On-demand search: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/rapidApi.ts createRapidApiAdapter (89-118): the activejobs adapter's markets become ['intl','cn'] with isEnabledFor('cn') = the same gate; INGEST_ACTIVEJOBS_CN_DAILY_CALLS (MKT-3A, default 0) is raised to 20 by default only while the gate is open. For cn the request carries role text only: the taxonomy zh label and its English label as two title variants, and locationText 'China' or the English city name; never a user id, resume text, e-mail or free-typed sentence longer than the role (strip to the planner's role text). JSearch stays off for cn (M-6) and LinkedIn is not a provider.
